body.text: 假設一座晶圓廠的工程師使用製程管理系統：

items: 不相關的人不能讀取客戶的晶片設計圖，這是 Confidentiality。
製程參數不能被未授權人員偷偷修改，這是 Integrity。
生產時系統必須正常提供所需資料，這是 Availability。
重要參數變更必須能追溯操作者及核准紀錄，這涉及 Non-repudiation。
機密資料經由網路傳輸時，需要適當保護，避免以 Cleartext 形式被第三方讀取。

body.text: 這五項並非彼此獨立。例如，具有正確身分認證的加密連線，可以同時協助保護傳輸資料的機密性與完整性。

sections.heading: 二、C01｜機密性 Confidentiality

body.text: M01-01 · CIA 三要素
1. 什麼是機密性？
機密性，就是只有被授權的人或系統，才能存取或知悉特定資訊。
假設你是一家半導體公司的研發主管，掌握下一代製程的技術資料。
你可能允許以下人員有不同的權限：

items: 製程工程師可以讀取自己負責的製程資料。
研發主管可以查看更完整的技術資訊。
外包設備維護人員只能取得維修所需的最小資料。
未經授權的人員不能讀取這些資料。

body.text: 機密性的重點並不是「所有資料都不能被別人看到」，而是誰能看到什麼資料，應由其授權決定。
NIST 對 Confidentiality 的定義聚焦於維持資訊存取與揭露的授權限制，也涵蓋個人隱私和專有資訊。
2. 臺灣半導體產業：為什麼晶片設計與製程資料需要機密性？
假設某半導體公司具有一份尚未公開的先進製程配方，這份資料對競爭對手具有極高價值。
假如員工將配方轉寄到私人信箱，問題就不只是公司內部管理不佳，還可能涉及營業秘密保護。
法律依據：《營業秘密法》第 2 條
營業秘密有三項法定要件：
1. 秘密性：不是相關領域一般人所知的資訊。
2. 經濟價值：因為保密，而具有實際或潛在的經濟價值。
3. 合理保密措施：所有人確實採取適當保密措施。
因此，企業可以透過身分驗證、存取權限、文件分級、保密契約與加密機制，建立合理保密措施。這些措施也是經濟部智慧財產局所列舉的保密實務。
真實企業依據：台積電資訊安全政策

台積電[2023年報](https://investor.tsmc.com/static/annualReports/2023/english/pdf/2023_tsmc_ar_e_ch5.pdf)公開揭露ISO 27001與客戶資訊保護；[2024年客戶資訊保護說明](https://esg.tsmc.com/en-US/articles/298)則呈現評估稽核、系統設計、安全控制及機制檢討。這些是特定年度的企業公開實務；本文沒有取得並核驗2026年全部有效證書，不能把其ISO/IEC 15408廠址認證與ISO27001混用。
這說明在半導體產業，機密性不只是資訊部門的事情，而是企業維持競爭優勢的重要條件。
3. 美國矽谷科技業：工程師為什麼不能任意讀取生產資料？
假設一家矽谷 AI 公司儲存客戶上傳的商業文件。工程師雖然具有系統維護職責，仍不代表可以自由閱讀所有客戶文件。
一套合理的系統會限制資料存取、保護儲存與傳輸，並記錄敏感操作。
技術標準：NIST CSF 2.0

items: PR.DS-01：保護儲存中資料的機密性、完整性與可用性。
PR.DS-02：保護傳輸中資料的機密性、完整性與可用性。

body.text: 這是可供企業採用的網路安全框架，並非所有矽谷公司一律依法必須取得的認證。
加州法規：California Civil Code §1798.81.5(b)
對適用本條的企業，要求依個人資訊性質建立並維持合理的資訊安全程序與措施，保護個人資訊免於未授權存取、使用、修改或揭露。這是法律要求，與 NIST 的技術建議屬於不同層級。
4. 臺灣金融業：客戶資料為什麼不能隨便查閱？
假設某銀行行員因私人好奇，查詢並向朋友透露某位客戶的存款餘額。
即使資料完全正確、銀行系統也正常運作，這個情境仍涉及機密性。
法規依據：金管會《金融控股公司及銀行業內部控制及稽核制度實施辦法》
第 12 條將客戶資料保密納入金融機構內部控制的政策與作業程序，第 25 條則明定資訊安全專責單位應督導落實資訊安全制度，確保機密性、完整性與可用性。
5. CEH 必須掌握的判斷方法
遇到下列敘述，優先思考 Confidentiality：

items: Unauthorized disclosure：未授權揭露
Information leakage：資訊洩漏
Eavesdropping：竊聽
Data exfiltration：資料外洩或竊取
Unauthorized reading：未授權讀取

body.text: 關鍵問題：是不是不應該看到資料的人，取得了資料？
如果答案是肯定的，核心安全性質通常就是機密性。

sections.heading: 三、C02｜完整性 Integrity

body.text: M01-01 · CIA 三要素
1. 什麼是完整性？
完整性，就是資料沒有遭到未經授權或不正當的修改、破壞，並能維持應有的正確狀態。
這與機密性完全不同。
假設一份銀行轉帳指示原本是：

body.text: 如果駭客完全沒看過其他客戶資料，卻成功修改了這筆轉帳內容，最直接受到破壞的就是 Integrity。
NIST 對 Data Integrity 的定義，是資料在建立、傳輸、儲存後，未遭到未授權修改的性質。
要特別理解：完整性不等於禁止任何修改。
銀行客戶經過適當身分驗證，正常修改自己的通訊地址，是符合完整性的授權操作。駭客冒充客戶，任意修改地址，才是完整性問題。
2. 臺灣半導體：製程參數被竄改會發生什麼事？
假設一座晶圓廠的設備參數原本由工程師核定，但攻擊者取得設備控制權，偷偷更改參數。
設備可能繼續運轉，機密文件也未必外洩，但生產結果可能因此偏離預期。
這種事件核心涉及製程資料與控制命令的完整性；若進一步造成停機，也會影響可用性。
產業標準依據：SEMI E187 — Specification for Cybersecurity of Fab Equipment
SEMI E187 是針對半導體晶圓廠設備的資安標準，關注作業系統支援、網路安全、端點保護與安全監控等面向。
SEMI 官方說明，相關標準工作由臺灣技術委員會與北美、日本等技術委員會合作推動。這些設備安全控制有助於減少未授權操作和惡意軟體導致的製程風險。
這裡要區分：SEMI E187 是設備資安要求，具體的製程參數簽核、變更授權與資料完整性驗證，仍須由企業的製程及設備控制制度落實。
3. 美國矽谷：軟體更新為什麼要驗證完整性？
假設一家美國軟體公司原本發布正常的安裝程式，但下載站上的檔案被攻擊者替換成惡意版本。
使用者下載後，會以為取得的是官方軟體。
工程上可以利用：

items: Cryptographic Hash： 產生資料摘要，協助偵測檔案是否改變。
Digital Signature： 驗證檔案來源及簽署後的完整性。
Access Control： 限制誰能修改正式發布檔案。
Change Management： 透過審核與版本管理追蹤變更。

body.text: NIST CSF 2.0 的 PR.DS-01 實作範例包含驗證軟體簽章，以確認軟體完整性。
這裡有一個很重要的技術區別：
普通雜湊可以幫助判斷兩份檔案是否相同；但如果攻擊者可以同時替換檔案與公布的雜湊值，使用者仍可能受騙。因此，驗證用的摘要或簽章也需要可信的來源。
4. 臺灣金融業：金管會如何處理交易指示完整性？
以前述轉帳金額為例，金融機構除了確認登入者身分，也需要確認客戶實際輸入的交易內容，和後端收到的內容一致。
現行[《電子支付機構資訊系統標準及安全控管作業基準》](https://epa.org.tw/uploads/regulations/pdfs/01M47H2X8FK89E4RTGBCPV9WSW.pdf)第5、6條規範訊息防護，第11條第1款第4目要求辨識使用者輸入與系統接收的支付指示一致性。供稿引用的同名「辦法」已於2023年4月25日廢止；本處改採2026年9月29日版公會基準。
這份公會基準依《電子支付機構管理條例》第32條第2項訂定，適用範圍與一般銀行電子銀行業務規範不同。查核時先確認機構類型、交易種類、適用安全設計與版本，再把交易完整性控制對應到具體要求。
5. CEH 必須掌握的判斷方法
只要題目描述的是：

items: Unauthorized modification：未授權修改
Tampering：竄改
Data corruption：資料毀損
Unauthorized deletion：未授權刪除
Altered transaction：交易內容被修改

body.text: 就應優先檢查 Integrity。
關鍵問題：資料是否遭到未經授權的改變，或失去應有的可信狀態？

sections.heading: 四、C03｜可用性 Availability

body.text: M01-01 · CIA 三要素
1. 什麼是可用性？
可用性，就是有權使用系統的人，在需要的時間，能可靠地取得資料或使用服務。
假設你的銀行帳戶裡有錢，帳戶資料也完全正確，但你急著轉帳時，網路銀行卻一直無法登入。
這時候發生什麼問題？
資料不一定被偷，也不一定被修改，而是你無法在需要時使用服務。
這就是 Availability。
NIST 將 Availability 定義為確保資訊能被及時、可靠地存取與使用。
2. 臺灣半導體業：晶圓廠為什麼特別重視可用性？
假設一座晶圓廠的製造執行系統（Manufacturing Execution System, MES）突然無法運作。
工程師可能無法正常取得生產批次資訊、設備狀態或製程作業資料，進而影響工廠運作。
這時，核心問題是生產所需系統的 Availability。
在半導體產業，還必須考慮一個特別的情況：不只是電腦系統可用，還要確保設備、網路及製造流程之間能持續協作。
產業依據：
SEMI E187 的設備資安範圍涵蓋作業系統、網路安全、端點保護及安全監控。台積電公開的資訊安全措施也包括惡意軟體防護、網路區隔及防止病毒在設備和廠區之間擴散。這些控制有助於降低生產系統遭受資安事件中斷的風險。
3. 美國矽谷：雲端服務如何維持可用性？
假設一家矽谷 SaaS 公司提供企業級 AI 服務。

body.text: 技術標準：NIST CSF 2.0
PR.IR-03 要求達成正常及不利情況下的韌性目標，實作範例包括避免單點故障、負載平衡、備援儲存和備援電力。
PR.IR-04 則著重維持足夠的運算、儲存、電力和網路資源容量。
這些措施對應兩個概念：High Availability（高可用性）與 Resilience（韌性）。
高可用性著重減少服務中斷；韌性則進一步要求系統在故障或攻擊下，仍能維持必要功能並恢復運作。
4. 臺灣金融業：銀行服務中斷不只是 IT 問題
假設網路銀行受到大量惡意流量攻擊，使用者無法登入或轉帳。
這類 Denial-of-Service（DoS，阻斷服務）情境，核心影響通常是 Availability。
金管會《金融控股公司及銀行業內部控制及稽核制度實施辦法》第 12 條要求內部控制包含營運持續管理機制，第 25 條則涵蓋系統與服務的可用性及資安事件應變。
在實務上，會衍生兩個經常使用的指標：

rows: 系統發生中斷後，目標是在多久之內恢復服務？
系統復原時，最多可容忍遺失多長時間範圍的最新資料？例如RPO為15分鐘，目標是復原點與中斷時間相差不超過15分鐘。

body.text: 例如，銀行不只要思考系統如何重新啟動，也要確認交易紀錄是否正確恢復。這說明 Availability 與 Integrity 常常需要一起處理。
5. CEH 判斷重點
當題目出現 Service Disruption、DoS、DDoS、System Outage、Resource Exhaustion 或 Inaccessible System 時，應優先思考 Availability。
判斷問題：有權使用服務的人，是否無法在需要時取得服務？

sections.heading: 五、C04｜不可否認性 Non-repudiation

body.text: M01-07 · 安全治理與證據條件
1. 什麼是不可否認性？
不可否認性，就是透過可靠的證據，讓重要行為的發生、來源和責任歸屬能夠被驗證。
假設一家半導體公司有兩位工程師。
某天，一份重要製程文件被批准並送入正式生產環境。事後發現文件有問題，負責人卻說：
「這不是我核准的。」
公司應該如何確認？
光是看到資料庫裡出現他的名字，證據可能還不夠。
更完整的證據包括操作者身分、核准內容、操作時間、可信的簽章及受保護的稽核紀錄。
NIST 對 Non-repudiation 的說明，是建立足以抵抗當事人虛假否認特定行為的證據能力，包括文件建立、訊息傳送及資訊核准等行為。
2. 完整性與不可否認性有什麼不同？
假設有一份電子契約：

items: Integrity： 能確認契約內容沒有遭到不當修改。
Non-repudiation： 能提供可驗證證據，支持契約是由特定簽署者簽署。

body.text: 這是兩個相關但不同的判斷問題。
不可否認性在資訊安全架構中也常被視為完整性與真實性相關的延伸保證。

4. 三種產業的規範依據
臺灣半導體：製程變更的簽署與追溯
公司可以針對關鍵製程變更建立數位核准紀錄，結合簽章、身分驗證及不可任意更改的稽核紀錄。
[《電子簽章法》](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=J0080037)第2條定義電子簽章與數位簽章，第4條說明符合規定者的功能等同與法律效力。第6條的本人簽名或蓋章推定，要求主管機關許可憑證機構簽發的憑證，且憑證未逾有效期間及使用範圍；技術上驗章成功仍須核對這些法律條件。
美國矽谷：重要軟體發布的來源證明
軟體公司可利用數位簽章，使使用者驗證發布成品與簽署來源。NIST FIPS 186-5 將第三方可驗證的資料來源與完整性，列為 Non-repudiation 的核心性質。
臺灣金融業：電子交易的證據保存
現行電支公會基準第5、6條依適用的安全設計規範不可否認性，第10條就約定連結存款帳戶付款規定憑證簽驗章及相關私鑰保護。簽章、憑證與交易紀錄須配合實際交易類型查核；不能把已廢止辦法的第7–9條直接視為現行條號。
銀行業另有中華民國銀行商業同業公會全國聯合會於 2026 年 5 月 18 日公布的《金融機構使用電子簽名機制安全控管作業規範》，可作為銀行相關業務查核的專門依據。
5. CEH 判斷重點
當題目提到行為人否認簽署、否認發送訊息、交易責任歸屬、數位簽章證據或可驗證的簽署紀錄時，通常是在考 Non-repudiation。
要特別記得：Encryption、Hash 與 Digital Signature 並不代表同一件事。

body.text: M01-01 · 機密性與資料傳輸風險
1. 什麼是 Cleartext？
Cleartext（明文）就是資料保持可直接閱讀、理解的形式，沒有經過保護其內容的加密處理。
例如，銀行帳戶資料若以未加密的形式通過不可信網路，能攔截通訊的第三方就可能直接讀取內容。
NIST 資安術語將 Cleartext 描述為未加密資訊，並與 Plaintext 作為相關用語。

body.text: IETF 的RFC 8446是TLS 1.3的原始規格，已由2026年7月發布的[RFC 9846](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9846)取代。TLS提供身分驗證、機密性與完整性；HTTPS須正確驗證伺服器並建立TLS連線，端點、應用程式與金鑰管理仍須另行保護。
因此，HTTPS 不只是把 HTTP 換一個名稱，而是利用 TLS 建立受保護的通訊通道。
但還有兩個很容易被忽略的概念。
第一，Base64 不是加密。
假設密碼經過 Base64 編碼後再傳送，只要知道編碼方式，就能把它轉回原始內容。編碼主要是為了資料表示與傳輸相容性，不是用來提供機密性。
第二，資料是明文，不等於一定發生機密性事件。
例如，授權使用者在安全環境內閱讀已解密的文件，是正常的資料使用流程。安全問題取決於明文是否暴露在不適當的信任邊界，或讓未授權者取得。

body.text: 以下是新的教學情境，不是附件的原始考題。先回答問題，不必查資料，也先不公布標準答案。
某臺灣半導體公司與一家美國矽谷 AI 公司合作，建立自動化製程分析系統。雙方使用雲端平台交換設計資料，並由臺灣一家銀行提供專案融資。
合作期間發生五件事：
1. 美國 AI 公司一位沒有專案權限的工程師，讀取了臺灣半導體公司的機密設計文件。
2. 攻擊者成功更改 AI 系統傳送給晶圓廠的製程參數。
3. 雲端服務受到 DDoS 攻擊，造成晶圓廠無法取得即時分析結果。
4. 一位主管否認曾經核准某項重要製程變更，但系統保存了有效的數位簽章。
5. 雙方使用未加密的 HTTP 連線，傳送客戶的機密技術文件。
請你回答三個問題：
Q1. 這五件事各自最直接對應哪一個 C01–C05 觀念？第 5 件又主要威脅哪一個 CIA 安全目標？
Q2. 如果要求你針對第 2 件事設計完整性保護，你會選擇哪些控制措施？為什麼不能只靠資料加密？
Q3. 如果這個合作系統需要接受臺灣半導體客戶、美國企業客戶與臺灣金融機構的資安審查，你會分別引用哪三類法律或標準，作為設計與稽核依據？

sections.heading: 核心結論：駭客與倫理駭客的區別，不在使用什麼工具，而在是否取得有效授權、遵守測試邊界，以及如何處理測試結果

body.text: 同一個人使用同一套工具、執行相同的漏洞驗證方法，在不同的授權條件、行為目的與執行方式下，可能構成正當安全測試，也可能構成違反規範甚至觸法的行為。
我們要理解的並非單純的「白帽好、黑帽壞」，而是一套能讓安全測試具有可授權性、可控制性、可驗證性與可問責性的治理架構。
先把五個重要原則記住：

items: Authorization（授權）： 誰有權允許測試？允許誰測試？
Scope（範圍）： 允許測試哪些資產、系統與資料？
ROE（Rules of Engagement）： 可以採取哪些行為、何時測試、何時必須停止？
Evidence（證據）： 如何證明漏洞確實存在，且測試過程受到控制？
Remediation（改善）： 如何將發現轉化為安全修補、風險降低和再次驗證？

body.text: 這套思路以 NIST SP 800-115《Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment》的規劃、測試、評估與報告要求為基礎，並結合 OWASP、MITRE ATT&CK 及臺美產業規範。

案例背景： 假設臺灣某大型半導體製造商委託一家美國矽谷資安公司，評估其客戶設計資料交換平台。該平台與一家受金管會監理銀行的供應鏈融資系統交換必要資訊。

sections.heading: 二、C06｜Ethical Hacking：為什麼需要倫理駭客？

body.text: 1. 從攻擊者的角度，驗證防禦系統是否有效
想像你負責半導體公司的資訊安全。
公司已經購買防火牆、端點防護系統、身分驗證服務，也建立了數十項安全政策。
管理階層問你：
「我們到底安全嗎？」
你可能回答：
「我們有防火牆，有多因素驗證，也符合資訊安全政策。」
但是，這並不能充分證明系統能抵抗真實攻擊。
原因是：
控制措施存在，不等於控制措施有效。
例如，系統雖然要求登入，但工程師可能仍能透過 API 取得其他客戶的機密設計檔案。
這就是倫理駭客要解決的問題。
Ethical Hacking 是在經過適當授權與控制的條件下，使用攻擊者可能採取的技術，尋找並驗證安全弱點，以改善組織的防禦能力。
2. 三種不同的安全工作

NIST SP 800-115第4章介紹目標識別與分析，第5章介紹包含滲透測試的弱點驗證技術；滲透測試可進一步驗證可利用性。
3. 如何使用 OWASP 與 MITRE ATT&CK？
假設半導體平台有一個 API：
`GET /api/designs/1234`

OWASP：告訴我們應驗證什麼安全控制。
OWASP API Security Top 10 2023 的 API1：Broken Object Level Authorization（BOLA），就是典型的物件層級授權失效。
其核心要求是：當 API 使用物件識別碼存取資料時，必須驗證當前使用者是否有權對該物件執行指定操作。

例如，T1190「Exploit Public-Facing Application」描述攻擊者利用對外服務弱點取得初始存取的技術。

C06 的重點：倫理駭客的成果不是「成功入侵了多少系統」，而是為組織建立多少可信、可採取行動的安全證據。

sections.heading: 三、C07｜Authorization：授權到底是什麼？

body.text: 1. 有公司委託，不代表可以測試公司所有系統
回到半導體案例。
假設委託書只寫：
「請協助進行資訊安全滲透測試。」
這句話可以證明雙方有合作意願，但對實際測試而言，資訊仍然不足。
例如，研究人員可能不知道：

items: 是否可以測試正式生產環境？
是否包括雲端服務商管理的基礎設施？
是否允許觸碰其他客戶的資料？
是否能嘗試修改製程設備參數？
是否允許執行可能中斷服務的測試？

body.text: 因此，專業測試不只需要取得授權，還需要把授權轉化為明確的操作權限。
NIST 對 ROE 的定義指出，交戰規則應在測試開始前建立，並授權測試團隊執行其中明定的活動。
2. Authorization 有兩種不同的意思
這是進階學習時必須區分的地方。

rows: 資產擁有者或適當權責人，允許研究人員執行特定安全測試
系統允許使用者存取哪些資料與功能

body.text: 例如，研究人員得到半導體公司授權，測試客戶資料平台是否存在存取控制問題。
他的測試授權是有效的，但測試目的正是驗證系統內的存取授權是否能被繞過。
OWASP WSTG-ATHZ-02 專門處理存取授權繞過測試，包括同權限使用者之間的水平越權，以及不同權限角色之間的垂直越權。
3. 臺灣與美國法律如何看待未經授權的存取？
中華民國：《刑法》第 358–360 條
第 358 條處理無故以帳密、破解保護措施或利用系統漏洞入侵他人電腦的行為。第 359 條涉及無故取得、刪除或變更他人電磁紀錄而致生損害；第 360 條涉及無故以電腦程式或其他電磁方式干擾他人電腦而致生損害。
不同條文具有不同構成要件，實際行為須分別判斷。
美國：Computer Fraud and Abuse Act（CFAA），18 U.S.C. §1030
CFAA 第 (a)(2) 項涵蓋特定未經授權或超越授權的電腦存取並取得資訊的行為；第 (a)(5) 項則涉及特定未經授權造成電腦損害的行為。
美國司法部 2022 年修訂的 CFAA 起訴政策，對符合定義的善意安全研究設有不起訴方向，但它是聯邦檢察機關的起訴政策，並非授予研究者無限制測試權。
4. 為什麼要書面授權？
書面文件可以確定授權者、測試者、目標、期限、允許活動及責任分工。
常見文件包括授權書（Authorization Letter）、工作說明書（Statement of Work, SOW）、交戰規則（ROE）及保密協議（NDA）。
這些文件功能不同：NDA 處理保密義務，SOW 處理交付範圍，ROE 處理測試操作，而適當的書面授權則建立明確的測試許可。
C07 最重要的一句話：有權委託測試的人，必須對被測資產具有相應的授權權限；有權測試一項資產，不代表有權測試與它連接的所有資產。

sections.heading: 四、C08｜Scope 與 Rules of Engagement：把授權落實成可執行規則

body.text: 1. Scope 是「測試邊界」，ROE 是「執行規則」
假設某銀行只授權測試網路銀行的測試環境。
這就是 Scope。
但研究人員還需要知道：
「可以在幾點測？每秒最多多少請求？能不能進行權限提升驗證？如果系統異常，誰有權要求停止？」
這些屬於 ROE。
在 NIST SP 800-115 的架構中，ROE 可以同時包含範圍與操作規則；這裡把 Scope 單獨區分，是為了讓學習與管理更清楚。
2. 一份專業 ROE 的六大控制面向
依據 NIST SP 800-115 Appendix B，原始範本涵蓋目的、範圍、風險、測試人員、時間、通訊、目標系統、允許／禁止行為、資料處理、報告及簽署等項目。以下將其整理成六大實務控制面向。

rows: 授權者、測試團隊、權責主管、簽署與有效期限
允許及排除的網域、IP、API、雲端帳號、資料與設備
可用工具、攻擊驗證方式、禁止操作與操作限制
測試時段、負載限制、停止條件、恢復程序
SOC、系統負責人、緊急聯絡及事件升級程序
日誌、敏感資料處理、漏洞報告、修補及複測

body.text: 3. 半導體產業：為什麼不能照一般 IT 方式測試所有設備？
這是非常值得深入研究的案例。
NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3《Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security》附錄 C.3.4 記載，一次工業控制系統的 ping sweep（主機探測）曾導致晶片製造系統停止運作，造成約 50,000 美元的晶圓損失。同一節也記錄了工業網路探測造成機械手臂非預期動作的案例。
這說明一般 IT 網路中常被視為相對低風險的探測，到了 OT（Operational Technology，營運技術）環境，可能具有完全不同的後果。

body.caption: 同樣是安全測試，風險並不相同
body.description: 產業安全要求取決於實際資產與風險，不代表所有IT或OT系統都有相同限制。兩欄比較考量，不表示OT可以忽略資料安全與服務復原。

items.body:
辦公網路、網站、一般應用程式
主要考量：服務可用性、資料安全、系統復原

製造設備、控制系統、製程網路
額外考量：設備安全、製程穩定、實體損失

body.text: 在臺灣半導體設備安全領域，SEMI E187《Specification for Cybersecurity of Fab Equipment》針對半導體生產設備提出作業系統支援、網路安全、端點防護及安全監控等基本要求。其公開適用範圍主要涉及搭載 Windows 或 Linux 的設備運算裝置，並未涵蓋所有 PLC、SCADA 及相關感測／致動控制裝置。
臺灣亦已建立以 SEMI E187 為基礎的半導體設備資安查核與驗證制度。
將 NIST 800-82 的 OT 風險觀念與 SEMI E187 的設備安全要求結合，專業團隊可以將 ROE 設計為：
生產設備先進行安全影響評估；優先選擇被動監控、離線分析或經驗證的測試環境；正式設備上的主動測試須經額外核准，且具有停止與復原措施。
這是根據上述標準所做的風險導向設計，而不是宣稱 SEMI E187 逐字要求所有設備採用相同測試程序。
C08 的關鍵：ROE 不是行政文件，而是一套控制安全測試行為的操作規則。

sections.heading: 五、C09–C13｜駭客類型：從名稱分類，進一步理解行為、目的與能力

body.text: 這五個概念最適合一起學習，因為它們其實在描述不同的分類維度。
C09｜White Hat：白帽駭客
白帽駭客是經過適當授權，以改善系統安全為目的，並遵守約定測試規則的安全研究或測試人員。
假設一家矽谷科技公司聘請研究人員評估產品的 API 安全。
研究人員取得書面授權，使用公司提供的測試帳號，確認是否存在權限繞過問題，最後提交弱點報告並協助複測。
這是典型的 White Hat Hacking。
判斷重點不在於研究人員有多厲害，而在於其行為是否符合授權、範圍與目的。
實務依據： NIST SP 800-115 第 6–8 章，關注測試規劃、執行、報告及修補活動。
C10｜Grey Hat：灰帽駭客
灰帽駭客通常指沒有明確惡意目的，卻在未取得授權或未完全遵守測試規則的情況下進行安全探索的人。
例如，某研究人員發現銀行網站可能有弱點。
他沒有取得銀行授權，就進一步存取其他客戶的資料，隨後私下通知銀行：「我幫你們找到漏洞了。」
即使他最初的目的是改善安全，也不會因此自動取得測試權限。
這裡應區分三個命題：

rows: 因此已取得該企業的測試授權
行為是否違法，需要依適用法律與事實判斷

body.text: 前面提及的美國 DOJ 2022 年 CFAA 善意研究起訴政策，正好說明「研究動機」、「執行方式」、「起訴政策」與「法律授權」是不同層次。
C11｜Black Hat：黑帽駭客
黑帽駭客通常以未經授權方式入侵系統，並具有竊取、勒索、破壞或其他惡意目的。
例如，攻擊者利用半導體供應鏈入口取得資料，將機密技術文件轉售給第三方。
其核心問題包括未授權存取與不當取得資訊。
在臺灣法律體系中，應依實際行為分別檢視《刑法》第 358–360 條，以及資料符合營業秘密要件時的《營業秘密法》相關規定。
C12｜Blue Hat：藍帽駭客
這個詞需要特別注意，因為在不同資料中並沒有完全一致的定義。
有些資安教材將 Blue Hat 指為受邀協助產品上市前安全測試的外部專家；另一些資料則把它用於具有報復動機的攻擊者。

例如，[ESET詞彙](https://help.eset.com/glossary/en-US/hacker.html)使用受邀顧問的定義；[ORE Catapult 2025年報告](https://cms.ore.catapult.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/PN844-RPT-006_WP4-Cybersecurity-and-Autonomous-Systems-Report_Rev2.pdf)的Table 7則列出報復型與受邀測試型兩種用法。這些是各來源的術語分類，不是CEH官方統一的法律或身分類別。
Microsoft 也有名為 BlueHat 的安全研究交流活動，但不能因此把 BlueHat 會議的參加者，直接等同於某一類具有固定法律或技術身分的駭客。
CEH 遇到 Blue Hat 選項時，應結合題幹和指定教材理解，不應單靠顏色做出判斷。
C13｜Script Kiddie：依賴現成工具的低經驗攻擊者
Script Kiddie 通常指技術理解較有限、主要依賴他人開發工具或程式進行操作的人。
重要的是，技術能力與授權狀態不是同一件事。
一位初學者在經過授權的實驗環境使用 Nmap，可以是在正常學習安全測試；一位資深工程師未經授權入侵系統，仍可能屬於不當行為。
所以 Script Kiddie 主要描述技術能力或使用方式，而不是直接判定是否合法。
更精確的分類模型
與其記住帽子的顏色，更重要的是用三個互相獨立的維度理解一個行為：

headers: 未取得有效授權或超出範圍
rows: 以改善安全為主要目的
典型 White Hat 行為
常見 Grey Hat 情境
以竊取、破壞或勒索為目的
若利用測試權限從事未被允許的惡意行為，該行為已不受原授權涵蓋
典型 Black Hat 行為

body.text: 技術能力可以再獨立加入分析，不應與這個矩陣混為一談。
這也是為什麼 CEH 要學白帽、灰帽、黑帽，但真正進入企業安全治理時，應用行為、權限、目的與證據描述事實，而不能只用顏色標籤替代分析。

sections.heading: 六、C14｜Penetration Testing：滲透測試究竟在驗證什麼？

body.text: 滲透測試不等於單純「試著駭進去」。
它是一個在事先設定的安全條件下，建立可重複的測試過程，驗證系統弱點、分析可能影響、提供改善證據的技術活動。
1. 弱點掃描與滲透測試的科學差異
假設弱點掃描工具發現一台網站伺服器使用了有已知漏洞的元件版本。
這是重要線索，但尚不能直接推論攻擊一定成功。
可能的原因包括：系統已套用修補但未更新版本字串、弱點僅存在於特定設定，或攻擊所需的前提條件並不存在。
因此我們需要驗證。

body.name: validationevidence
body.caption: 從潛在弱點到可驗證的改善
body.description: 箭頭表示驗證與改善的工作順序；受控驗證使用已授權資產與測試資料，不以增加破壞或大量取得真實資料作為證明。

items.title: 觀察到潛在弱點
items.body: 掃描、設定分析、原始碼審查

items.title: 建立可驗證假說
items.body: 在指定條件下，這個弱點是否可被利用？

items.title: 受控驗證
items.body: 使用授權資產與測試資料，採取足以確認弱點的操作

items.title: 記錄觀察與限制
items.body: 證據、影響、測試條件、未測試範圍

items.title: 修補與再次驗證
items.body: 確認弱點關閉，且正常業務沒有受到破壞

body.text: 這與科學研究的邏輯非常接近：觀察、假說、實驗、證據、結論，以及可重現性。
但滲透測試還多一項特殊要求：測試本身必須受到風險限制。
2. NIST SP 800-115：滲透測試的階段
NIST SP 800-115 第 5.2 節把滲透測試的主要技術工作分成 Planning、Discovery、Attack 與 Reporting；報告工作並非只在最後才開始，而是可以貫穿整個過程。

rows: 了解系統、服務及可能弱點
在核准範圍內驗證可利用性
分析影響、修補優先順序與限制

body.text: 3. 進階案例：驗證半導體設計資料平台的 BOLA
假設我們有兩個由測試團隊控制的帳號：
帳號 A 屬於測試客戶 A；帳號 B 屬於測試客戶 B。
兩者各自擁有一份人工建立、沒有真實營業秘密的設計文件。
我們要驗證：
帳號 A 是否可能在未獲授權的情況下，讀取帳號 B 的測試文件？
這是一個明確、可驗證的安全假說。
OWASP WSTG-ATHZ-02 指出，水平越權測試會檢查同一權限層級但不同使用者的資源是否能被彼此存取。
如果帳號 A 能讀取 B 的測試資料，就能建立弱點證據；不需要再下載所有真實客戶的文件。
還可以提出更深入的驗證問題：伺服器是否在每次存取資料時檢查權限，或只在使用者登入時檢查一次？
這會影響修補方法。
真正的問題可能不在前端頁面，而在後端 API 缺少物件層級授權檢查。
4. 如何衡量滲透測試的品質？
對研究與企業交付而言，可以使用下列模型：
測試價值 ≈ 可驗證且可採取行動的安全證據 ÷（測試成本與造成的附加風險）
這是協助思考的概念模型，並非 NIST 的官方計算公式。
有價值的報告，應讓工程團隊知道弱點發生的必要條件、實際影響、證據、修補方向與修補後如何複測。
C14 的關鍵：成功的滲透測試不以破壞程度衡量，而以可驗證的風險發現及改善成效衡量。

sections.heading: 七、C15｜弱點揭露、資訊保密與研究責任

body.text: 1. 找到弱點，不代表可以任意公開
假設研究人員在臺灣半導體公司的系統發現一項重大漏洞。
該漏洞可能讓其他客戶讀取未公開的晶片設計檔案。
研究人員擁有技術發現，不代表擁有客戶文件的處分權或公開權。
因此，漏洞研究必須同時管理兩種資訊：漏洞本身的技術細節，以及測試過程接觸到的敏感資料。
2. Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure（CVD）
CVD 是協調式弱點揭露。
它的基本思路是研究人員向適當的安全窗口回報弱點，讓供應商、研究人員及相關利害關係人協調驗證、修補、通知及公開時機。
OWASP《Vulnerability Disclosure Cheat Sheet》建議研究人員確認測試合法且已授權，尊重他人隱私，提供足夠的驗證與重現資訊，並避免在既有獎勵制度以外要求付款作為揭露條件。
一份實用的弱點報告可以長這樣：

rows: 已授權的設計資料測試 API
測試帳號 A、B 與指定資料
可能違反不同客戶之間的資料隔離
遮罩後的請求、回應與存取日誌
在後端建立物件層級授權檢查
A 無法取得 B 的資料，且合法存取仍正常

body.text: 其中 OWASP 的 API1:2023 明確指出，物件層級授權應在涉及用戶端提供之物件 ID 的資料存取操作中進行驗證。
3. 臺灣半導體的法律關聯
《營業秘密法》第 2 條將秘密性、因秘密性而具有的經濟價值，以及合理保密措施列為營業秘密的核心要件。
因此，企業在進行外部安全測試時，應透過資料分級、最小必要存取、保密約定、證據保存及交付控制，降低敏感技術資料的暴露風險。
4. 美國矽谷公司的弱點回報制度
矽谷科技公司常透過 Vulnerability Disclosure Policy（VDP）或 Bug Bounty 計畫定義研究者可測試的資產與行為。
OWASP 指出，這類計畫應明確交代 Scope、測試規則、回報方式及適用的 safe harbor 條件；並可透過符合 RFC 9116 的 `security.txt` 協助研究者找到安全回報窗口。
需要注意，Bug Bounty 是特定條件下的測試邀請，不是對企業所有系統開放無限制測試。
5. 金融業的資訊保護與監督責任
《金融控股公司及銀行業內部控制及稽核制度實施辦法》第 24 條要求適用機構設置資訊安全專責單位，第 25 條則規範資安制度規劃、風險控管及安全事件通報應變等職責。
金融機構在委託外部滲透測試時，可以將這些法規要求轉化為承包商測試流程、敏感客戶資料保護、資安事件通報與改善追蹤的管理要求。
銀行公會網站於2026年3月5日公告《金融機構資通系統與服務供應鏈風險管理規範》，附件版本為v2026.2.13；公告日與版本日各有其意義，是金融供應鏈治理應一併查核的自律規範。
C15 的關鍵：弱點發現不是工作的終點。如何處理證據、通報風險、完成修補，才決定研究成果是否真正改善安全。

sections.heading: 八、C16｜攻擊目的與測試目的：同樣的技術，為什麼可能具有不同性質？

body.text: CEH 有時會把 Ethical Hacking 與 DoS、資料竊取及散布惡意軟體放在同一道選擇題。
這些題目通常不是在問技術是否強大，而是在問其主要目的。
1. 用 MITRE ATT&CK 理解攻擊行為

rows: 未授權存取、權限提升等
系統資源耗盡或服務中斷
透過 C2 通道外洩資料

body.text: 以上對應均以 MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise 技術頁面為依據。
這裡要注意一個非常重要的觀念：
MITRE ATT&CK 描述的是攻擊者行為與技術，不負責決定某次安全測試是否已獲授權。
研究團隊可以在受控條件下模擬部分 ATT&CK 技術，以評估防禦控制，但是否能執行，仍由測試授權與 ROE 決定。
2. 以金融業 DDoS 情境說明
假設銀行想知道自己的網路銀行，是否能承受大量惡意請求。
這個目的本身可以是正當的安全驗證。
但如果團隊直接對正式網路銀行發動大量流量攻擊，導致客戶無法進行正常交易，就可能產生嚴重營運風險，也可能超出授權。
更合理的測試設計，是先確認需要驗證的是哪一項防護能力。
例如：流量清洗服務的偵測能力、限流規則、應變程序，或系統在特定流量情境下的承載能力。
再依風險與適用的 ROE，選擇模擬環境、受控負載或經核准的服務提供者測試機制。

案例：
臺灣一家半導體設備公司委託美國資安公司測試供應鏈管理平台，測試團隊取得書面授權，可測試指定的測試環境。
測試期間發生以下情況：
A. 工程師使用 OWASP 方法，發現測試帳號可能讀取另一個帳號的測試文件。
B. 工程師發現正式環境也可能存在相同問題，於是直接登入正式系統驗證，但正式系統不在授權範圍內。
C. 工程師發現設備管理網路與企業辦公網路相連，決定使用主動掃描工具探測設備控制器，但 ROE 並未允許測試 OT 網路。
D. 測試團隊只使用人工測試資料，完整記錄弱點證據，向企業安全負責人回報並提出修補建議。
E. 另一位研究人員發現銀行的電子交易平台存在疑似安全問題，未取得授權即嘗試存取其他客戶的交易資料，之後表示自己的目的只是幫助銀行。
請回答：

items: 1. 分類判斷： A–E 哪些行為符合有效授權與測試邊界？哪些需要重新取得核准？哪些最接近 White Hat 或 Grey Hat 的典型情境？
2. 標準應用： 針對 C 的 OT 測試風險，應如何運用 NIST SP 800-82 與 SEMI E187 的不同角色，重新設計測試程序？
3. 安全工程： 針對 A 的弱點，你會使用 OWASP 的哪一項測試概念？可能如何對應 MITRE ATT&CK？為什麼兩者不能互相替代？
4. 法令與治理： 如果 B 的正式系統包含美國公司的客戶資料，而 E 的銀行位於臺灣，你會分別先檢視哪些法律、授權文件與自律規範？
5. 研究方法： 如何設計最小充分驗證（Minimum Sufficient Validation），證明弱點存在，同時限制資訊暴露、設備異常及對第三方的影響？

sections.heading: 1 | How the five concepts relate

body.text: C01–C03 are the three core information-security objectives, collectively called the CIA triad. C04 concerns evidence and attribution, while C05 concerns data exposure closely related to confidentiality.

body.name: ciaobjectives
body.caption: CIA objectives and two related concepts
body.description: The three upper items are parallel security objectives. Non-repudiation concerns evidence; cleartext concerns data representation and exposure. They are not a fourth and fifth CIA objective.

items.title: C01 · Confidentiality
items.body: Who may read the information?

items.title: C02 · Integrity
items.body: Is the content trustworthy?

items.title: C03 · Availability
items.body: Can authorized users use it when needed?

items.title: C04 · Non-repudiation
items.body: Can evidence support attribution afterward?

items.title: C05 · Cleartext
items.body: Is readable data exposed across an inappropriate trust boundary?

body.text: Suppose an engineer uses a process-management system in a semiconductor fab:

items: People unrelated to a project must not read the customer’s chip designs: confidentiality.
Unauthorized personnel must not secretly change process parameters: integrity.
Production must receive the required data when needed: availability.
Important parameter changes must be traceable to their operators and approval records: non-repudiation.
Confidential data sent over a network needs suitable protection against third parties reading it as cleartext.

body.text: These concepts interact. For example, a correctly authenticated encrypted connection can help protect both the confidentiality and integrity of data in transit.

sections.heading: 2 | C01: Confidentiality

body.text: M01-01 · The CIA triad
1. What is confidentiality?
Confidentiality means that only authorized people or systems may access or learn particular information.
Imagine that you manage research and development at a semiconductor company and hold technical information about its next-generation process.
Different people may receive different permissions:

items: Process engineers may read the process data they are responsible for.
The R&D manager may view more comprehensive technical information.
Contracted equipment-maintenance personnel receive only the minimum information necessary for maintenance.
Unauthorized personnel must not read this information.

body.text: Confidentiality is about deciding who may see which information according to authorization. It does not require making every piece of information inaccessible to everyone.
NIST defines confidentiality around preserving authorized restrictions on access and disclosure, including personal privacy and proprietary information.
2. Taiwan’s semiconductor industry: why protect chip designs and process data?
Suppose a semiconductor company holds an unpublished advanced-process recipe that would be highly valuable to competitors.
An employee forwarding that recipe to a personal mailbox may raise trade-secret protection issues as well as internal-management concerns.
Legal basis: Article 2 of Taiwan’s Trade Secrets Act.
A trade secret must meet three statutory requirements:
1. Secrecy: the information is not generally known to people involved with that type of information.
2. Economic value: its secrecy gives it actual or potential economic value.
3. Reasonable secrecy measures: the owner has actually adopted reasonable protective measures.

Authentication, access permissions, document classification, confidentiality agreements and encryption can contribute to reasonable secrecy measures. Taiwan’s Intellectual Property Office also identifies such practices.
Published corporate practice: TSMC’s information-security policies.

TSMC’s [2023 annual report](https://investor.tsmc.com/static/annualReports/2023/english/pdf/2023_tsmc_ar_e_ch5.pdf) discusses ISO 27001 and customer-information protection. Its [2024 customer-information article](https://esg.tsmc.com/en-US/articles/298) describes assessment and audit, system design, security controls and mechanism review. These disclosures belong to particular reporting years. This lesson has not obtained and verified every certificate valid in 2026; ISO/IEC 15408 site certification must not be conflated with ISO 27001.
In semiconductor manufacturing, confidentiality supports the company’s competitive position and requires participation beyond the IT department.
3. Silicon Valley technology companies: why can’t engineers freely read production data?
Suppose an AI company stores business documents uploaded by customers. An engineer’s system-maintenance responsibilities do not automatically authorize reading every customer document.
A suitable system restricts data access, protects storage and transmission, and records sensitive operations.
Technical framework: NIST CSF 2.0.

items: PR.DS-01: protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of data at rest.
PR.DS-02: protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of data in transit.

body.text: Organizations can adopt this cybersecurity framework. It is not a certification that every Silicon Valley company is legally required to obtain.
California law: Civil Code §1798.81.5(b).

For businesses within its scope, this provision requires reasonable security procedures and practices appropriate to the nature of personal information, protecting it against unauthorized access, use, modification or disclosure. A legal requirement and NIST technical guidance have different authority.
4. Taiwan’s financial industry: why restrict customer-record access?
Suppose a bank employee, out of personal curiosity, looks up a customer’s deposit balance and discloses it to a friend.
This concerns confidentiality even if the data is accurate and the bank’s systems operate normally.
Regulatory basis: the FSC’s Implementation Rules of Internal Audit and Internal Control System of Financial Holding Companies and Banking Industries.

Article 12 includes customer-data confidentiality in internal-control policies and procedures. Article 25 assigns the dedicated information-security unit responsibility for overseeing implementation and ensuring confidentiality, integrity and availability.
5. Reasoning cues for CEH questions
Consider confidentiality first when the scenario describes:

items: Unauthorized disclosure: information revealed without permission.
Information leakage: protected information escapes its intended boundary.
Eavesdropping: another party listens to communication.
Data exfiltration: information is extracted or stolen.
Unauthorized reading: someone reads information without permission.

body.text: Ask: did someone who should not have access obtain the information?
If so, confidentiality is usually the primary security property involved.

sections.heading: 3 | C02: Integrity

body.text: M01-01 · The CIA triad
1. What is integrity?
Integrity means that information remains in its intended correct state, protected from unauthorized or improper modification and destruction.
Integrity asks a different question from confidentiality.
Suppose a bank-transfer instruction originally contains the following amount:

body.name: transactiontampering
body.caption: Transaction integrity: unauthorized amount change
body.description: The two states compare the original instruction with tampered content, not two executed transfers. The amount changes from NT$10,000 to NT$100,000.

items.title: Original instruction · NT$10,000
items.body: Transfer to the specified recipient

items.title: Tampered instruction · NT$100,000
items.body: The amount was maliciously changed

body.text: Even if an attacker never reads other customers’ records, successfully changing this transfer instruction directly compromises integrity.
NIST describes data integrity as the property that data has not been changed without authorization after its creation, transmission or storage.
Integrity does not prohibit every change.

A properly authenticated customer changing their own mailing address is an authorized operation consistent with integrity. An attacker impersonating that customer and changing the address without permission creates an integrity problem.
2. Taiwan’s semiconductor industry: what happens when process parameters are altered?
Suppose engineers approved equipment parameters at a fab, but an attacker gains control of the equipment and secretly changes them.
The equipment might keep running and confidential documents might remain undisclosed, while production results deviate from expectations.
The primary issue concerns the integrity of process data and control commands. If the incident also stops production, availability is affected too.
Industry reference: SEMI E187 — Specification for Cybersecurity of Fab Equipment.
SEMI E187 addresses cybersecurity of semiconductor fab equipment, including operating-system support, network security, endpoint protection and security monitoring.

SEMI describes standards work involving its Taiwan, North America and Japan technical committees. Equipment-security controls can help reduce process risks caused by unauthorized operations and malware.
SEMI E187 concerns equipment cybersecurity. The company’s own process and equipment controls must implement specific parameter approvals, change authorization and integrity verification.
3. Silicon Valley: why verify software-update integrity?
Suppose a US software company releases a legitimate installer, but an attacker replaces the file on its download site with a malicious version.
Users may download it believing it is the official software.
Engineering controls include:

items: Cryptographic hash: produce a digest to help detect file changes.
Digital signature: verify the signing source and integrity since signing.
Access control: restrict who may modify release artifacts.
Change management: track changes through review and version control.

body.text: NIST CSF 2.0 implementation examples for PR.DS-01 include verifying software signatures to establish integrity.
The trustworthiness of the verification information matters:

A plain hash helps compare files. If an attacker can replace both the file and its published hash, however, the user can still be deceived. Verification digests or signatures therefore need a trusted source.
4. Taiwan’s financial industry: protecting transaction-instruction integrity
For the transfer example, an institution must establish both who logged in and whether the instruction received by its backend matches what the customer actually entered.

Articles 5 and 6 of the current [Electronic Payment Institutions Information System Standards and Security Control Guidelines](https://epa.org.tw/uploads/regulations/pdfs/01M47H2X8FK89E4RTGBCPV9WSW.pdf) address message protection. Article 11, paragraph 1, item 4 addresses consistency between payment instructions entered by users and received by the system. The similarly named regulations cited in the supplied text were repealed on April 25, 2023; this lesson uses the September 29, 2026 association guidelines.

These association guidelines are established under Article 32, paragraph 2 of the Act Governing Electronic Payment Institutions. Their scope differs from banking rules for electronic banking. Identify the institution, transaction type, security design and version before mapping integrity controls to specific requirements.
5. Reasoning cues for CEH questions
Check whether the question describes:

items: Unauthorized modification.
Tampering.
Data corruption.
Unauthorized deletion.
An altered transaction.

body.text: These cues point first to integrity.
Ask: was information changed without authorization, or did it lose its intended trustworthy state?

sections.heading: 4 | C03: Availability

body.text: M01-01 · The CIA triad
1. What is availability?
Availability means that authorized users can reliably obtain information or use services when needed.
Suppose your bank account contains money and its records are accurate, but you cannot log in to online banking when you urgently need to make a transfer.
What failed in this situation?
The information need not have been stolen or changed. The immediate problem is that you cannot use the service when needed.
This is an availability problem.
NIST defines availability around timely and reliable access to and use of information.
2. Taiwan’s semiconductor industry: why does fab availability matter?
Suppose a fab’s manufacturing execution system, or MES, suddenly stops working.
Engineers may lose access to production-lot information, equipment status and process-operation data, affecting factory operations.
The primary issue is the availability of systems required for production.
In semiconductor manufacturing, availability also requires equipment, networks and manufacturing processes to keep working together, beyond individual computers remaining operational.
Industry context:

SEMI E187 addresses operating systems, networks, endpoint protection and security monitoring. TSMC has also publicly described malware protection, network segmentation and limiting virus propagation between equipment and fabs. Such controls can reduce the risk of security incidents interrupting production systems.
3. Silicon Valley: how do cloud services maintain availability?
Suppose a Silicon Valley SaaS company provides an enterprise AI service.

body.text: Technical framework: NIST CSF 2.0.
PR.IR-03 addresses resilience in normal and adverse conditions. Implementation examples include avoiding single points of failure, load balancing, redundant storage and backup power.
PR.IR-04 focuses on maintaining sufficient compute, storage, power and network capacity.
These measures connect high availability with resilience.
High availability focuses on reducing service interruptions. Resilience additionally concerns maintaining necessary functions and recovering during failures or attacks.
4. Taiwan’s financial industry: service interruption extends beyond IT
Suppose malicious traffic overwhelms online banking, preventing users from logging in or transferring funds.
The primary impact of this denial-of-service, or DoS, scenario is usually availability.
Article 12 of the FSC banking internal-control rules includes business-continuity management. Article 25 covers the availability of systems and services and security-incident response.
Two practical objectives help plan recovery:

rows: How soon after an interruption should service be restored?
How much recent data loss is tolerable? For an assumed RPO of 15 minutes, the recovery point should be no more than 15 minutes before the interruption.

body.text: A bank needs to establish both how to restart systems and whether transaction records have been restored correctly. Availability and integrity often require coordinated controls.
5. Reasoning cues for CEH questions
Service disruption, DoS, DDoS, system outage, resource exhaustion and an inaccessible system point first to availability.
Ask: are authorized users unable to obtain the service when they need it?

sections.heading: 5 | C04: Non-repudiation

body.text: M01-07 · Security governance and evidence conditions
1. What is non-repudiation?
Non-repudiation uses reliable evidence to make important actions, their origin and attribution verifiable.
Suppose a semiconductor company employs two engineers.
An important process document is approved and enters production. A problem is later discovered, and the responsible person says:
“I did not approve this.”
How should the company verify what happened?
The person’s name appearing in a database may be insufficient evidence.
A stronger evidence package includes operator identity, the approved content, operation time, a trustworthy signature and protected audit records.
NIST describes non-repudiation as establishing evidence that resists false denial of actions such as creating a document, sending a message or approving information.
2. How does non-repudiation differ from integrity?
Consider an electronic contract:

items: Integrity: verify that the contract content has not been improperly changed.
Non-repudiation: provide verifiable evidence supporting attribution to a particular signer.

body.text: These are related but distinct questions.
Information-security frameworks also treat non-repudiation as an assurance related to integrity and authenticity.
3. How can digital signatures establish evidence?

body.name: signatureevidence
body.caption: Digital signatures: creating and verifying evidence
body.description: A typical conceptual flow; actual computation differs by algorithm. Attribution also requires trusted certificates, private-key protection, time and audit evidence. A name in a database is insufficient.

items.title: Original electronic document
items.body: For example, an approved process-change record

items.title: Generate a cryptographic hash
items.body: Map the document to a fixed-length digest

items.title: Sign using the private key
items.body: Create a signature with a key controlled by the signer

items.title: Verify signature and identity
items.body: Use the public key with certificates, time and audit records

body.text: A digital signature can provide evidence verifiable by a third party. Attribution also requires trustworthy certificates, private-key protection and a complete signing process.
4. References for the three industries
Taiwan’s semiconductor industry: signing and tracing process changes.
A company can maintain digital approvals for critical process changes, combining signatures, identity verification and audit records protected against arbitrary modification.

Article 2 of Taiwan’s [Electronic Signatures Act](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=J0080037) defines electronic and digital signatures. Article 4 addresses functional equivalence and legal effect when the statutory requirements are met. Article 6 presumes a personal signature or seal only when the certificate comes from an authorized certification authority and remains within its validity period and permitted scope. Successful technical verification still requires checking these legal conditions.
Silicon Valley: proving the source of important software releases.
Software companies can sign releases so users can verify artifacts and signing sources. NIST FIPS 186-5 describes third-party-verifiable origin and integrity as properties supporting non-repudiation.
Taiwan’s financial industry: preserving electronic-transaction evidence.

Articles 5 and 6 of the current electronic-payment association guidelines address non-repudiation according to the applicable security design. Article 10 addresses certificate signing and verification and private-key protection for linked-deposit-account payments. Check signatures, certificates and records against the transaction type; Articles 7–9 of the repealed regulations are not current clause references.

The Bankers Association also lists its Security Control Guidelines for Financial Institutions Using Electronic Signature Mechanisms, announced on its website on May 18, 2026, as a specialized reference for relevant banking operations.
5. Reasoning cues for CEH questions
Denial of signing or sending a message, disputed transaction attribution, digital-signature evidence and verifiable signing records usually concern non-repudiation.
Encryption, hashes and digital signatures provide different capabilities.

sections.heading: 6 | C05: Cleartext transmission and information exposure

body.text: M01-01 · Confidentiality and data-in-transit risk
1. What is cleartext?
Cleartext is information in a directly readable, understandable form without encryption protecting its contents.
For example, a third party able to intercept unencrypted bank-account information on an untrusted network may read its contents directly.
NIST’s glossary describes cleartext as unencrypted information and identifies plaintext as a related term.
2. Why is HTTPS generally more suitable than HTTP for sensitive data?

body.text: RFC 8446 was the original TLS 1.3 specification. [RFC 9846](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9846), published in July 2026, supersedes it. TLS provides authentication, confidentiality and integrity. HTTPS requires correct server validation and TLS establishment; endpoints, applications and key management still need protection.
HTTPS uses TLS to establish a protected communication channel.
Two distinctions are easy to overlook.
First, Base64 is not encryption.
A password encoded with Base64 can be decoded by anyone who knows the encoding. Encoding supports data representation and transport compatibility; it does not provide confidentiality.
Second, the presence of cleartext does not by itself prove a confidentiality incident.

An authorized user reading a decrypted document in a secure environment is part of normal use. The security issue depends on whether readable data crosses an inappropriate trust boundary or reaches an unauthorized party.

sections.heading: 9 | Understanding check: integrate the five concepts

body.text: This is a new teaching scenario, not an original question from the attachment. Try answering before consulting references; model answers are withheld.

A Taiwanese semiconductor company partners with a Silicon Valley AI company to build an automated process-analysis system. They exchange design information through a cloud platform, with project financing provided by a Taiwanese bank.
Five events occur:
1. An engineer at the AI company, without project authorization, reads the semiconductor company’s confidential design documents.
2. An attacker changes process parameters sent by the AI system to the fab.
3. DDoS interrupts the cloud service, preventing the fab from obtaining real-time analysis results.
4. A manager denies approving a critical process change, but the system retains a valid digital signature.
5. The companies transmit confidential customer technical documents through unencrypted HTTP.
Answer three questions:
Q1. Which C01–C05 concept most directly matches each event? Which CIA objective does event 5 primarily threaten?
Q2. Which controls would you choose to protect integrity against event 2? Why is data encryption alone insufficient?

Q3. If the system is reviewed by Taiwanese semiconductor customers, US enterprise customers and Taiwanese financial institutions, which three categories of laws or standards would you cite for design and audit requirements?

sections.heading: C06–C16 | Ethical hacking depends on authorization, boundaries and handling of results

body.text: The same person using the same tools and vulnerability-verification method may perform legitimate security testing or violate rules and potentially laws, depending on authorization, purpose and conduct.
The useful framework goes beyond labeling white hats good and black hats bad: security testing needs valid authority, operational control, verifiable evidence and accountability.
Keep five principles in view:

items: Authorization: who has authority to permit the test, and who may perform it?
Scope: which assets, systems and data may be tested?
Rules of engagement, or ROE: which actions are permitted, when may testing occur, and when must it stop?
Evidence: how can the team demonstrate the weakness and a controlled testing process?
Remediation: how do findings lead to fixes, lower risk and verification?

body.text: This approach uses the planning, testing, assessment and reporting guidance in NIST SP 800-115, Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment, together with OWASP, MITRE ATT&CK and Taiwanese and US industry requirements.

sections.heading: 1 | The C06–C16 knowledge map

body.text: This chapter retains the C06–C16 concept identifiers and mainly relates to M01-03, Ethical Hacking, Authorization and Rules of Engagement. Formal sub-identifiers for C12 and C13 and cross-chapter details for C16 remain unverified. These concept identifiers do not represent newly published course lessons.

rows: How far may an authorized test proceed?
What makes conduct typical white-hat behavior?
How should good intentions without authorization be assessed?
What distinguishes malicious intrusion from legitimate testing?
Which different meanings does blue hat have?
How do technical ability and legality differ?
How do findings lead to verification and remediation?
How should a discovered weakness be reported responsibly?
Where are the boundaries for DoS, data theft and malware testing?

body.text: One continuing scenario connects the concepts.

Scenario: a large Taiwanese semiconductor manufacturer hires a Silicon Valley cybersecurity company to assess its customer-design data exchange platform. The platform exchanges necessary information with a supply-chain financing system at an FSC-regulated bank.
This is a hypothetical teaching scenario, not a claim that any particular company has a vulnerability.

sections.heading: 2 | C06: Why ethical hacking is needed

body.text: 1. Assess defenses from an attacker’s perspective
Imagine that you manage information security at a semiconductor company.
The company has purchased firewalls, endpoint protection and identity services and established dozens of security policies.
Management asks:
“Are we actually secure?”
You might answer:
“We have firewalls and multifactor authentication, and we comply with our information-security policies.”
This does not adequately demonstrate resistance to real attacks.
The reason is straightforward:
The existence of a control does not establish its effectiveness.
For example, a system may require login while its API still lets an engineer obtain another customer’s confidential design files.
Ethical hacking addresses this gap in evidence.
Ethical hacking uses techniques an attacker might employ, under appropriate authorization and controls, to identify and verify weaknesses and improve organizational defenses.
2. Three different security activities

rows: Are specified policies and requirements followed?
Review documents, controls and execution evidence
Can weaknesses be exploited, and with what impact?
Controlled exploitation verification and risk analysis

body.text: These activities overlap but do not replace one another.
Chapter 4 of NIST SP 800-115 addresses target identification and analysis. Chapter 5 addresses vulnerability-validation techniques, including penetration testing to verify exploitability.
3. Using OWASP and MITRE ATT&CK
Suppose the semiconductor platform exposes an API:
`GET /api/designs/1234`
A researcher suspects that changing the file identifier might expose another customer’s designs.
Two bodies of knowledge can help in different ways.
OWASP identifies application controls that should be checked.
API1 in the OWASP API Security Top 10 2023 is Broken Object Level Authorization, or BOLA.
Whenever an API uses an object identifier to access data, it must verify whether the current user may perform the requested operation on that object.
MITRE ATT&CK helps describe how real adversaries operate.
For example, T1190, Exploit Public-Facing Application, describes exploiting weaknesses in externally accessible services to gain initial access.
Their perspectives differ:

body.name: securityframeworks
body.caption: OWASP and MITRE ATT&CK: complementary perspectives
body.description: These are parallel perspectives. NIST SP 800-115 adds assessment planning, execution, evidence and reporting. An ATT&CK identifier does not authorize a test.

items.title: OWASP
items.body:
Starts with application weaknesses and security controls
What should be tested, verified and improved?

items.title: MITRE ATT&CK
items.body:
Starts with observed adversary behavior
How do attackers act, and can defenses detect them?

body.text: NIST SP 800-115 adds methods for planning and executing tests, preserving evidence and reporting results.
C06 focuses on the trustworthy, actionable security evidence delivered to an organization, rather than counting systems compromised.

sections.heading: 3 | C07: What authorization means

body.text: 1. A company engagement does not authorize testing every company system
Return to the semiconductor scenario.
Suppose the engagement letter says only:
“Please assist with an information-security penetration test.”
This indicates an intention to collaborate but leaves important operational questions unanswered.
For example, the researcher may not know:

items: May the production environment be tested?
Does permission include infrastructure managed by a cloud provider?
May the team access other customers’ information?
May it attempt to change manufacturing-equipment parameters?
Are potentially disruptive tests permitted?

body.text: Professional testing needs authorization translated into explicit operational permissions.
NIST defines ROE as rules established before testing that authorize the team to perform specifically defined activities.
2. Two meanings of authorization
Keep the following distinction when studying more advanced security topics.

rows: An asset owner or appropriate authority permits specified security testing
The data and functions that the system permits a user to access

body.text: A researcher may be authorized by the semiconductor company to test its customer-data platform for access-control weaknesses.
That testing permission can be valid even though the purpose is to determine whether the application’s access authorization can be bypassed.
OWASP WSTG-ATHZ-02 addresses authorization-bypass testing, including horizontal access between users with the same privileges and vertical access between different roles.
3. Unauthorized access under Taiwanese and US law
Taiwan: Criminal Code Articles 358–360.

Article 358 addresses intrusion without justification using another person’s credentials, defeating computer protections or exploiting a system weakness. Article 359 addresses obtaining, deleting or altering another person’s electromagnetic records without justification and causing damage. Article 360 addresses interference without justification with another person’s computer through programs or other electromagnetic means and resulting damage.
The provisions have different elements; assess actual conduct against each applicable provision.
United States: the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, or CFAA, 18 U.S.C. §1030.
Subsection (a)(2) covers specified unauthorized or excessive access that obtains information. Subsection (a)(5) addresses specified conduct causing computer damage without authorization.

The DOJ’s 2022 CFAA charging policy directs prosecutors not to charge conduct meeting its definition of good-faith security research. It is a federal prosecution policy, not an unlimited grant of testing permission.
4. Why document authorization in writing?
Written documents identify the authorizer, tester, targets, validity period, permitted activities and responsibilities.
Common documents include an authorization letter, statement of work or SOW, ROE and a nondisclosure agreement or NDA.
They serve different purposes: an NDA governs confidentiality, an SOW defines deliverables, ROE governs testing operations, and appropriate written authorization establishes clear testing permission.
C07: the person commissioning a test must have corresponding authority over the target assets. Permission to test one asset does not extend automatically to every connected asset.

sections.heading: 4 | C08: Making scope and ROE operational

body.text: 1. Scope defines the testing boundary; ROE defines operating rules
Suppose a bank authorizes testing only in its online-banking test environment.
This defines the scope.
The researcher still needs answers to questions such as:
“At what times may we test? What request rate is allowed? May we verify privilege escalation? Who can require us to stop if the system behaves abnormally?”
These belong in the ROE.
NIST SP 800-115 allows ROE to include both scope and operating rules. Separating scope here helps explain and manage their different functions.
2. Six practical control areas for ROE

Appendix B of NIST SP 800-115 includes objectives, scope, risks, personnel, schedule, communications, target systems, permitted and prohibited actions, data handling, reporting and signatures. The following table groups these into six practical areas.

rows: Authorizer, testing team, accountable managers, signatures and validity period
Included and excluded domains, IPs, APIs, cloud accounts, data and equipment
Permitted tools and verification methods, prohibited actions and operating limits
Testing windows, load limits, stop conditions and recovery procedures
SOC, system owners, emergency contacts and escalation
Logs, sensitive-data handling, findings, remediation and retesting

body.text: 3. Why semiconductor equipment cannot all be tested like general IT
The following historical incident makes the risk concrete.

Appendix C.3.4 of NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3, Guide to Operational Technology Security, records a ping sweep on an industrial-control network that halted a chip-manufacturing control system and destroyed approximately US$50,000 worth of wafers. It also records a separate industrial-network probing incident that caused unexpected movement of a robotic arm.
A probe considered relatively low risk in an ordinary IT network can have very different consequences in operational technology, or OT.

body.name: itotrisks
body.caption: Security testing carries different risks
body.description: Requirements depend on actual assets and risks, rather than imposing identical restrictions on every IT or OT system. The comparison does not imply that OT can ignore data security or recovery.

items.title: Enterprise IT systems
items.body:
Office networks, websites and general applications
Key concerns: service availability, data security and recovery

items.title: Fab OT systems
items.body:
Manufacturing equipment, control systems and process networks
Additional concerns: equipment safety, process stability and physical loss

body.text: SEMI E187, Specification for Cybersecurity of Fab Equipment, addresses operating-system support, network security, endpoint protection and security monitoring. Its public scope primarily covers equipment computing devices running Windows or Linux; it does not cover all PLCs, SCADA systems or associated sensor and actuator devices.
Taiwan also has a semiconductor-equipment cybersecurity assessment and certification scheme based on SEMI E187.
Combining NIST SP 800-82’s OT risk guidance with SEMI E187’s equipment-security requirements suggests ROE such as:

Assess safety impacts before testing production equipment. Prefer passive monitoring, offline analysis or a validated test environment. Active testing of production equipment requires additional approval, stop conditions and recovery measures.
This is a risk-based engineering design derived from the references, not a claim that SEMI E187 prescribes identical testing procedures for every device.
C08: ROE is an operational mechanism for controlling testing conduct, beyond its role as documentation.

sections.heading: 5 | C09–C13: Distinguish conduct, purpose and ability

body.text: These five terms belong together because they describe different classification dimensions.
C09 | White hat
A white-hat researcher or tester acts under appropriate authorization, aims to improve security and follows agreed testing rules.
Suppose a Silicon Valley company hires a researcher to assess its product APIs.
The researcher obtains written permission, uses company-provided test accounts, checks for authorization bypass, reports findings and assists with retesting.
This is typical white-hat conduct.
The key question concerns compliance with authorization, scope and purpose, rather than how technically impressive the researcher is.
Practical reference: NIST SP 800-115 Chapters 6–8 address planning, execution, reporting and mitigation activities.
C10 | Grey hat
Grey hat commonly describes security exploration without clear malicious intent but without authorization or full adherence to testing rules.
For example, a researcher suspects a weakness in a bank website.
Without permission, the researcher accesses other customers’ data and later privately tells the bank, “I found a vulnerability for you.”
An initial intention to improve security does not automatically grant testing permission.
Distinguish three propositions:

rows: The researcher wants to help improve security
Legality depends on the applicable law and facts

body.text: The DOJ’s 2022 CFAA policy illustrates the distinction between motivation, conduct, charging policy and legal authorization.
C11 | Black hat
Black hat commonly describes unauthorized intrusion with theft, extortion, destruction or another malicious purpose.
For example, an attacker obtains information through a semiconductor supply-chain entry point and sells confidential technical documents to a third party.
The central issues include unauthorized access and improper acquisition of information.
In Taiwan, assess the conduct against Criminal Code Articles 358–360 and, when the information meets the statutory definition, relevant Trade Secrets Act provisions.
C12 | Blue hat
This term has no fully consistent meaning across sources.
Some educational sources use blue hat for external experts invited to test products before release; others use it for attackers motivated by revenge.

The [ESET glossary](https://help.eset.com/glossary/en-US/hacker.html) uses the invited-consultant meaning. Table 7 of the [ORE Catapult 2025 report](https://cms.ore.catapult.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/PN844-RPT-006_WP4-Cybersecurity-and-Autonomous-Systems-Report_Rev2.pdf) records both revenge-motivated and invited-testing meanings. These are source-specific classifications, not a uniform official CEH legal or identity category.
Microsoft also runs a security-research event called BlueHat. Attendance does not assign a fixed legal or technical hacker category to its participants.
For a CEH question containing blue hat, interpret the scenario and assigned materials rather than deciding solely from the color.
C13 | Script kiddie: limited experience and reliance on ready-made tools
Script kiddie commonly describes a person with limited technical understanding who primarily uses tools or programs developed by others.
Technical ability and authorization are different dimensions.
A beginner using Nmap in an authorized lab may be learning security testing appropriately. An experienced engineer intruding without permission may still act improperly.
The term primarily describes ability or tool use; it does not independently determine legality.
A more precise classification model
Use three independent dimensions to describe conduct:

headers: No valid authorization or outside scope
rows: Malicious activity not permitted by the engagement falls outside its authorization

body.text: Analyze technical ability separately from this purpose-and-authorization matrix.
CEH introduces white, grey and black hats, while enterprise governance needs descriptions of actual conduct, permissions, purpose and evidence rather than color labels alone.

sections.heading: 6 | C14: What penetration testing verifies

body.text: Penetration testing involves more than simply trying to break in.
It establishes a repeatable process under predefined safety conditions to verify weaknesses, analyze potential impacts and provide evidence for improvement.
1. The evidence distinction between scanning and penetration testing
Suppose a scanner reports that a web server uses a component version associated with a known vulnerability.
This is an important clue but does not establish that exploitation will succeed.
The system might have a backported fix without a changed version string, the weakness might depend on a particular configuration, or the necessary preconditions might be absent.
Verification is therefore necessary.

body.name: validationevidence
body.caption: From a potential weakness to verified improvement
body.description: Arrows show the assessment and remediation workflow. Controlled verification uses authorized assets and test data; greater damage or collecting real customer data is not required as proof.

items.title: Observe a potential weakness
items.body: Scanning, configuration analysis or source review

items.title: Form a testable hypothesis
items.body: Can this weakness be exploited under the specified conditions?

items.title: Perform controlled verification
items.body: Use authorized assets and test data, doing enough to confirm the weakness

items.title: Record observations and limits
items.body: Evidence, impact, test conditions and untested scope

items.title: Remediate and retest
items.body: Confirm closure while legitimate business operations remain functional

body.text: The reasoning resembles scientific work: observation, hypothesis, experiment, evidence, conclusion and reproducibility.
Penetration testing adds a critical constraint: the verification activity itself must remain within risk limits.
2. Penetration-testing phases in NIST SP 800-115
Section 5.2 describes Planning, Discovery, Attack and Reporting. Reporting can run throughout the process rather than beginning only after all technical work ends.

rows: Define objectives, authorization, ROE and risks
Understand systems, services and potential weaknesses
Analyze impacts, remediation priorities and limitations

body.text: 3. Advanced scenario: verify BOLA in a design-data platform
Suppose the testing team controls two accounts:
Account A belongs to test customer A; account B belongs to test customer B.
Each owns an artificial design document containing no real trade secrets.
The verification question is:
Can account A read account B’s test document without access authorization?
This is a specific, testable security hypothesis.
OWASP WSTG-ATHZ-02 describes horizontal authorization testing between different users at the same privilege level.
If A can read B’s test data, the team has evidence of the weakness. It need not download all real customers’ documents.
A further question is whether the server checks permission on every data access or only once at login.
This affects remediation.
The underlying problem may be missing object-level authorization in the backend API rather than in the frontend page.
4. Assessing penetration-test quality
A conceptual model for research and enterprise delivery is:
Testing value ≈ verifiable, actionable security evidence ÷ (testing cost and additional risk introduced)
This is a reasoning aid, not an official NIST calculation.
A useful report explains the necessary conditions, observed impact, evidence, remediation direction and how to verify the fix.
C14: evaluate testing by verifiable risk findings and effective improvement rather than the damage it causes.

sections.heading: 7 | C15: Disclosure, confidentiality and research responsibility

body.text: 1. Discovering a weakness does not grant permission to publish everything
Suppose a researcher discovers a serious weakness in a Taiwanese semiconductor company’s system.
It might let one customer read another customer’s unpublished chip designs.
Owning the technical discovery does not grant ownership of, disposal rights over or publication rights to customer documents.
Research must manage both vulnerability details and sensitive information encountered during testing.
2. Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure, or CVD
CVD means coordinated vulnerability disclosure.
Researchers report to an appropriate security contact so the vendor, researcher and stakeholders can coordinate verification, remediation, notification and publication timing.

OWASP’s Vulnerability Disclosure Cheat Sheet recommends lawful, authorized testing, respect for privacy, sufficient verification and reproduction information, and avoiding demands for payment as a disclosure condition outside established reward schemes.
A practical finding report might contain:

rows: Test accounts A and B and specified data
Possible failure of isolation between customers
Redacted requests, responses and access logs
Enforce object-level authorization in the backend
A cannot obtain B’s data, while permitted access remains functional

body.text: OWASP API1:2023 specifically calls for object-level authorization checks in data-access operations involving object IDs supplied by clients.
3. Legal connection for Taiwan’s semiconductor industry
Article 2 of the Trade Secrets Act identifies secrecy, economic value arising from secrecy, and reasonable secrecy measures as the core requirements.

External assessments should use data classification, minimum necessary access, confidentiality agreements, evidence preservation and controlled delivery to limit exposure of sensitive technical information.
4. Vulnerability-reporting programs at Silicon Valley companies
Technology companies commonly define permitted assets and activities through a Vulnerability Disclosure Policy, or VDP, or a bug-bounty program.
OWASP recommends clear scope, testing rules, reporting methods and applicable safe-harbor conditions. A `security.txt` file following RFC 9116 can help researchers find the reporting contact.
A bug-bounty invitation has specific conditions and does not authorize unrestricted testing of every company system.
5. Financial-sector information protection and oversight

Article 24 of Taiwan’s banking internal-control rules requires a dedicated information-security unit for applicable institutions. Article 25 addresses security planning, risk control and incident notification and response responsibilities.

Institutions commissioning external penetration tests can translate these responsibilities into contractor procedures, protection of sensitive customer data, incident notification and remediation tracking.

The Bankers Association announced its financial-institution ICT and service supply-chain risk-management rules on March 5, 2026; the attachment version is v2026.2.13. The announcement date and document-version date have different meanings. These self-regulatory rules are an additional reference for financial-sector supply-chain governance.
C15: handling evidence, communicating risk and completing remediation determine whether a discovery improves security.

sections.heading: 8 | C16: Distinguish attack purpose from testing purpose

body.text: CEH questions sometimes contrast ethical hacking with DoS, data theft and distributing malware.
The question usually concerns primary purpose rather than technical sophistication.
1. Describing adversary behavior with MITRE ATT&CK

rows: Unauthorized access, privilege escalation and related effects

body.text: These references use the official MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise technique pages.
Keep the following distinction:
ATT&CK describes adversary behavior and techniques. It does not determine whether a particular test has permission.
A research team may simulate selected techniques under controlled conditions to assess defenses, but authorization and ROE determine whether it may do so.
2. A banking DDoS scenario
Suppose a bank wants to establish whether online banking can withstand large volumes of malicious requests.
That objective can be legitimate security validation.
Directly generating large attack traffic against production banking could, however, stop customer transactions, create serious operational risk and exceed authorization.
First identify the defense capability that needs validation.
Examples include detection by a traffic-scrubbing service, rate limits, response procedures or capacity under a specified traffic scenario.
Then select a simulated environment, controlled load or approved provider testing mechanism according to risk and ROE.
Article 25 of Taiwan’s banking internal-control rules assigns CIA oversight and incident notification and response to the dedicated security unit, consistent with these risk-control objectives.
3. A decision model for legitimate security testing

body.caption: Authorization and risk gates for security testing
body.description: A practical model derived from NIST SP 800-115 and OWASP disclosure principles, not a legal-liability test. Both negative branches stop. Only the branch passing both gates proceeds to controlled verification and closure.

items.title: Is valid authorization in place?

items.title: No: do not perform it as an authorized test
items.body: Stop; obtain appropriate authorization and reassess

items.title: Yes: review the activity and risk
items.body: Does it comply with scope, ROE and risk limits?

items.title: No: stop and request an authorization change
items.body: This branch does not proceed to execution or closure

items.title: Yes: perform controlled verification and preserve evidence

body.text: The eleven concepts can be combined into practical engineering methods.

body.text: The table translates the cited requirements into governance recommendations. Testing focus and ROE design are risk-based engineering choices, not identical mandatory checklists prescribed by every reference.
Advanced question: why is testing a governance issue?
Penetration testing is often viewed primarily as technical work.

When it crosses departments, cloud providers, external consultants, financial data or manufacturing equipment, the team must determine who can authorize it, accept risk, stop work and own remediation.
Professional testing therefore needs three coordinated layers:

rows: Does the weakness exist, and how can it be verified?
OWASP WSTG, scanning and controlled tests
ROE, stop conditions, SOC and incident response
Who can approve, oversee and accept responsibility?
Authorization, risk management, audit and compliance

body.text: The shared objective is to keep potentially destructive technical activity within an authorized, auditable and controllable execution boundary.

sections.heading: 11 | Understanding check: semiconductor supply-chain assessment

body.text: Try reasoning independently before consulting references. These questions combine C06–C16.
Scenario:
A Taiwanese semiconductor-equipment company hires a US security company to assess its supply-chain platform. The team has written authorization for a specified test environment.
The following events occur:
A. An engineer uses OWASP methods and finds that one test account may read another account’s test document.
B. The engineer suspects the same weakness exists in production and logs into production to verify it, although production is outside the authorized scope.
C. The engineer discovers a connection between the equipment-management and office networks and decides to actively scan equipment controllers, although the ROE does not permit OT testing.
D. The team uses only artificial test data, records complete evidence, reports to the company’s security owner and recommends remediation.

E. Another researcher suspects a weakness in a Taiwanese bank’s transaction platform, attempts to access other customers’ transaction records without permission, and later says the purpose was to help.
Answer the following:

items: 1. Classification: which A–E activities comply with valid authorization and testing boundaries, which require new approval, and which resemble typical white-hat or grey-hat scenarios?
2. Standards: how should the different roles of NIST SP 800-82 and SEMI E187 inform a redesigned procedure for the OT risk in C?
3. Engineering: which OWASP testing concept applies to A? How might the observed behavior map to ATT&CK, and why do the two frameworks not replace one another?
4. Law and governance: if B’s production system contains a US company’s customer data and E’s bank is in Taiwan, which laws, authorization documents and industry rules would you examine first?
5. Research method: how would you design minimum sufficient validation to establish the weakness while limiting disclosure, equipment anomalies and effects on third parties?

body.text: The central capability is translating security-testing techniques into an authorized, risk-limited engineering process that produces trustworthy evidence and improves systems. This connects C06–C16 with cybersecurity research and operational governance.

sections.heading: 核心結論：資訊安全不是裝了多少防護工具，而是能否有效控制風險，並在資料生命週期結束時確實消除暴露風險

body.text: CEH v13 · M01-06 安全控制與縱深防禦 · 8 個核心觀念
這一單元有兩個核心問題：
第一，如何保護仍在使用的系統與資料？ 我們需要理解 Security Controls（安全控制），包括實體控制、技術控制、防火牆、防毒軟體與加密。
第二，當資料不再需要時，如何確保資料不會被還原？ 這涉及 Media Sanitization（媒體資料清理）、Purge、一般檔案刪除、儲存媒體回收及資料保存政策。
這兩個問題其實是同一件事的不同階段：

items.title: 驗證與證據
items.body: 驗證清理結果並保存證據，確保後續再利用、報廢或委外回收符合風險要求。

body.text: 特別重要的是，NIST 已於 2025 年 9 月 26 日正式發布 SP 800-88 Revision 2，取代 2014 年的 Revision 1。新版更重視企業整體媒體清理制度、清理方法的可信度及驗證，而不是只教你操作某種刪除工具。
因此，本次教學將保留 CEH 題目中的術語，同時使用現行 NIST 標準解釋它們的真正技術意義。

sections.heading: 一、完整知識地圖：C17–C24

body.text: 本次供稿將本單元八個觀念歸在 M01-06。其中 C17–C21 屬於安全控制分類及具體控制，C22–C24 則聚焦資料清理與不同資料處置行為的辨析。供稿所引用的課程附件將後三個觀念標示為待核子項；本文不據此宣稱已有獨立正式課次。

rows: 安全控制應如何分類與選擇？
實體保全與環境保護能防止什麼？
防火牆如何控制網路流量？
防毒軟體如何辨識及阻擋惡意程式？
加密能保護哪些安全性質？
如何清理資料，使進階復原方法不可行？
刪除檔案為什麼不等於清除實際資料？
硬體回收、資料封存與資料清理有何不同？

body.text: 我們仍採用三種真實產業的工程場景：臺灣半導體製造、美國矽谷雲端科技業，以及金管會監理下的臺灣金融機構；以 NIST、OWASP 和 MITRE ATT&CK 建立技術解釋，再用適用法律、產業標準與自律規範確認實務要求。

sections.heading: 二、C17｜Security Controls：安全控制到底是什麼？

body.text: 1. 白話理解：控制風險，而不是消滅所有風險
假設你負責一座先進晶圓廠的資安管理。
公司擔心三件事：

items: 外部攻擊者從網路入侵製造管理系統。
未授權人員進入設備機房。
報廢硬碟中的製程資料被第三方還原。

body.text: 你會怎麼辦？
對第一件事，可以設置防火牆、網路區隔及存取控制；第二件事需要門禁與保全；第三件事則需要資料清理及報廢管理。
這些都是 Security Controls（安全控制）。
它們不一定是軟體，也可能是人員、政策、設備、工作流程或技術機制。
NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 的安全控制目錄包括 Access Control（AC）、Physical and Environmental Protection（PE）、System and Communications Protection（SC）、Media Protection（MP）等控制家族。其維護版本已更新至 Release 5.2.0。
2. 安全控制必須同時理解三個分類維度
這是本章第一個核心觀念。

body.name: controlaxes
body.caption: 控制措施的三個分類軸
body.description: 三個軸可同時描述同一項控制，彼此不是先後步驟。 一項控制可能同時具有預防、偵測及其他作用；這些軸不是互斥分類。

items.title: A｜實作形式
items.body: Administrative：政策、制度、人員與程序／Technical：軟體、系統、網路與密碼學／Physical：門禁、保全、機房與實體設備

items.title: B｜控制功能
items.body: Preventive｜預防：降低事件發生機會／Detective｜偵測：發現事件或異常／Corrective｜矯正：修正已發現的問題／Recovery｜復原：恢復必要能力／Deterrent｜嚇阻：降低行為動機／Compensating｜補償：替代或補足其他控制

items.title: C｜保護目標
items.body: Confidentiality（機密性）、Integrity（完整性）、Availability（可用性），以及適用情境下的身分、可追溯性和隱私等要求。

body.text: 注意：這些維度可以交叉組合，並不是三套互相排斥的分類。一個控制也可能同時具有預防、偵測和其他作用。
3. 一個控制可以擁有多種功能

rows: 保護資料機密性；搭配適當模式可驗證完整性

body.text: 最後一列很重要。安全控制要依據實際機制分類。
使用加密清除金鑰，是邏輯／技術操作；將儲存晶片實體粉碎，則屬實體處置。兩者都可能用於媒體資料清理，但不代表使用相同的控制形式。
4. Defense in Depth：為什麼需要多層控制？
假設半導體公司只部署了防火牆。
如果內部員工直接將機密資料複製到隨身碟，防火牆可能根本看不到這個行為。
再假設公司只有機房保全。
如果攻擊者透過合法開放的 HTTPS 服務利用 API 弱點，保全也無法直接阻止。
所以，我們需要縱深防禦（Defense in Depth）。

body.name: defenselayers
body.caption: 四層縱深防禦
body.description: 外層包覆內層，多層控制共同保護核心資產。 多層防禦旨在避免單一控制失效就造成不可接受的後果；各控制仍須分別驗證有效性。
