body.caption: C25–C29 standards and concepts map
body.description: This learning map does not imply mandatory normative dependencies or certification order.

items.title: C25 | Risk management
items.body: Identify risks → analyze and assess → decide treatment.

items.title: C26 | ISO/IEC 27001
items.body: Specifies the information security management system an organization should establish.

items.title: C27 | ISO/IEC 27005
items.body: How is information security risk management performed in detail?

items.title: C28 | ISO/IEC 27002
items.body: Which security controls can be selected and implemented?

items.title: C29 | ISO/IEC 27701
items.body: How is a personal information and privacy information management system established?

body.text: The supplied manuscript maps these concepts to M01-07 and reports that they share one standards-comparison question using ISO/IEC 27701:2019. This article retains teaching about that historical version without claiming independent verification of the unavailable complete question.

First, note a version update: as of November 2026, ISO/IEC 27701:2025 is the current edition and has replaced the 2019 edition. We still explain the 2019 edition fully so that you can understand its role in the CEH question.

sections.heading: I. A comparison map of the five concepts and standards

rows: Management activities for identifying, assessing, treating, and monitoring risks
Requirements for an Information Security Management System (ISMS)
Guidance on information security risk management
Information security controls and implementation guidance
An extension standard in 2019; independent management-system requirements in 2025

body.text: ISO/IEC 27001 sets ISMS requirements. ISO/IEC 27005 supports risk management. ISO/IEC 27002 provides practical guidance on controls. ISO/IEC 27701 addresses privacy management for personally identifiable information (PII).
We begin with the basic concept of risk and develop an approach that an organization can carry out, audit, and use to support management decisions.

sections.heading: II. C25 | Information Security Risk Management: what does risk management manage?

body.text: 1. Distinguish threat, vulnerability, impact, and risk
Imagine that you manage cybersecurity for a Taiwanese semiconductor company.
One day, you discover that an equipment management system still uses insecure remote-management settings.
First distinguish the following concepts: asset, threat, vulnerability, impact and risk.

rows: An attacker might gain unauthorized access
Insufficient access protection for the remote-management interface
Equipment malfunction, downtime, or impaired process quality
A threat exploits a vulnerability and causes the losses described above

body.text: A vulnerability does not mean that a security incident has already occurred or that the risk must be high.
Describe it as a complete risk scenario.

Because an equipment management interface lacks appropriate access controls, an unauthorized person with network access might change equipment settings, causing process abnormalities or a production interruption.
This description makes the causal relationship explicit. It also provides a basis for collecting evidence, estimating risk, and designing controls.
NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1, Guide for Conducting Risk Assessments, connects threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood, impact, and risk assessment to provide management with information for risk decisions.
2. Risk assessment contains three distinct steps

body.name: riskassessment
body.caption: Three steps in risk assessment
body.description: Evaluation compares analysis results with established criteria.

items.title: Risk identification
items.body: Identify threats that may exploit vulnerabilities and affect important assets and business activities.

items.title: Risk analysis
items.body: Estimate incident likelihood, consequences and uncertainty to establish the level of risk.

items.title: Risk evaluation
items.body: Compare analysis results with predefined acceptance criteria to decide which risks require priority treatment.

body.text: ISO/IEC 27005:2022 addresses these stages in Clauses 7.2, 7.3, and 7.4, respectively.
In plain language:

items: Identification: what could go wrong?
Analysis: how likely is it, and how serious would its impact be?
Evaluation: can the organization accept this risk, or should it receive priority treatment?

body.text: These are different assessment activities. Calling all of them simply “doing a risk assessment” hides their distinct purposes.
3. How should we interpret Likelihood × Impact?
Security practice often uses a simplified model:
Risk Score = Likelihood × Impact
The OWASP Risk Rating Methodology provides a similar approach to risk scoring.
However, ISO/IEC 27005 does not require every organization to use one particular 5×5 risk matrix or to multiply two category numbers.
Consider an interactive example.

body.name: riskmatrix
body.caption: Risk score learning interaction
body.description: Teaching formula: score = L × I. L and I are ordinal integers from 1–5, not loss ratios. Thresholds: 1–4 low, 5–9 medium, 10–25 high. These thresholds are set by this teaching example, not official ISO values. The high-risk example calls for escalated review and priority treatment.

items.title: Likelihood L = 3
items.body: Ordinal scale from 1–5

items.title: Impact I = 5
items.body: Ordinal scale from 1–5

items.title: 3 × 5 = 15 / 25 | High risk
items.body: Illustrative thresholds; organizations define their own risk criteria.

body.text: A matrix can help prioritize risks, but it has a mathematical limitation: categories from 1 to 5 are usually ordinal scales, rather than quantities with fixed ratios. A risk score of 20 does not mean that actual losses must be twice those of a score of 10.

For low-frequency, high-consequence semiconductor OT incidents or financial transaction incidents, sufficient data may justify further consideration of event probability distributions, loss distributions, tail risk, dependent failures, and estimation uncertainty.
4. Inherent risk and residual risk: how much risk can controls reduce?
Distinguish two further concepts.
Inherent Risk: the level of risk in a scenario under assumptions that do not yet take particular controls into account.
Residual Risk: the risk remaining after relevant controls have been taken into account.
For example:
A manufacturing system is maintained through a remote-management connection.
The initial assessment in the example risk matrix is:

items: Likelihood: 3
Impact: 5
Risk Score: 15

body.text: The company then implements multifactor authentication, an isolated maintenance channel, time-limited authorization, operation logs, and anomaly monitoring.
After reassessment, if evidence supports reducing likelihood to 1 while impact remains 5, the residual risk score is 5.
This is a teaching assumption. A real assessment must establish that the relevant controls work effectively. Buying new security equipment does not automatically justify reducing the risk score.
5. Four common risk treatment strategies

rows: Do not undertake the activity that creates the risk
Stop unnecessary direct external connections to equipment
Use controls to reduce likelihood or impact
Share or transfer part of the consequences
Share some losses through contracts or insurance
Cyber insurance and supplier liability agreements
Retain residual risk through an authorized decision
The risk is within acceptance criteria and is approved by its owner

body.text: These are common categories of risk response. Even when insurance or a contract shares a risk, the company may retain legal obligations, loss of customer trust, and operational risks.

Also distinguish Risk Appetite, the types and amount of risk an organization is willing to take; Risk Tolerance, the permitted variation in risk for particular objectives; and Risk Acceptance, a formal decision to accept a particular risk.
6. The relationship with NIST CSF 2.0
NIST CSF 2.0's ID.RA, Risk Assessment, includes:

items: ID.RA-01: identify, validate, and record asset vulnerabilities.
ID.RA-04: record potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities.
ID.RA-05: use threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts to understand risk and establish priorities.
ID.RA-06: choose, plan, track, and communicate risk responses.

body.text: GV.RM, Risk Management Strategy, addresses the organization's risk management strategy, risk appetite, and decision criteria.
Risk assessment identifies and evaluates risks. Risk management also includes the decisions, treatment, tracking, and reassessment that follow.

sections.heading: III. C26 | ISO/IEC 27001:2022: what is an ISMS?

body.text: 1. An ISMS encompasses the organization's security management arrangements
ISMS stands for Information Security Management System.
Think of it as the complete set of arrangements through which an enterprise manages information security.
Alongside firewalls, encryption, and endpoint protection, it includes:

items: Security governance and allocation of responsibilities.
Security policies and objectives.
Risk assessment methods.
Selection and implementation of controls.
Personnel competence and necessary resources.
Internal audits and management reviews.
Continual improvement mechanisms.

body.text: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 is the international standard that defines ISMS requirements. An organization can establish its system against those requirements and seek third-party certification of conformity.
2. The overall structure of ISO 27001

headers: Management questions the organization must address
rows: Organizational scope, internal and external issues, interested parties
Top-management commitment, policy, authority, and responsibilities
Risk assessment, risk treatment, and information security objectives
Resources, competence, awareness, communication, and documentation
Conducting risk assessments, risk treatment, and operational controls
Monitoring and measurement, internal audits, and management review

body.text: The management cycle connects these activities:

body.name: pdcacycle
body.caption: PDCA continual improvement cycle
body.description: Cycle: Plan → Do → Check → Act → Plan. This teaching model does not mechanically partition every clause.

items.title: Plan
items.body: Scope, policy, risks and objectives.

items.title: Do
items.body: Controls and risk treatment.

items.title: Check
items.body: Audits, measurement and management review.

items.title: Act
items.body: Correction and management system updates.

body.text: PDCA is a teaching model for understanding continual improvement in management systems. It should not mechanically divide every ISO 27001 clause into four separate stages.
3. Two central risk clauses in ISO 27001
Clause 6.1.2 — Information Security Risk Assessment

The organization must establish a risk assessment process, including risk acceptance criteria, identification of risk owners, analysis of consequences and likelihood, risk evaluation, and retention of necessary documented information.
Clause 6.1.3 — Information Security Risk Treatment

The organization must select risk treatment options, determine necessary controls, compare them with Annex A, prepare a Statement of Applicability and a risk treatment plan, and obtain risk owners' approval of the plan and acceptance of residual risks.
Clauses 8.2 and 8.3 address actually performing risk assessment and risk treatment. These clauses are central to ISMS planning and operation.
4. What is a Statement of Applicability (SoA)?
SoA stands for Statement of Applicability.
Suppose that a semiconductor company decides to implement ISO/IEC 27001.
It does not follow that every Annex A control must be implemented without considering the context.
The organization should first determine the controls necessary for risk treatment, then compare them with Annex A to check that no necessary control has been omitted.
The SoA should record the necessary controls, reasons for including them, implementation status, and reasons for excluding Annex A controls.
For example:

rows: Protect manufacturing systems and customer design data
Equipment maintenance suppliers have system access
Depends on scope and actual use
Establish whether cloud services and related risks are present
May be excluded with sufficient justification

body.text: Control selection follows risk and documented justification.
5. Does ISO 27001 certification mean an organization cannot be hacked?
No.

Certification is a third-party assessment that a management system meets the standard's requirements within a defined scope. It does not provide a technical guarantee that all systems are free of vulnerabilities.
When reviewing a certificate, check at least:

items: The organization and business activities covered.
The standard edition and validity of the certificate.
Whether its scope includes the product or system being assessed.
Whether important controls have verifiable operating records.

body.text: ISO also distinguishes an organization's adoption of ISO/IEC 27001 from certification of conformity by a qualified certification body.
C26's central concept: ISO 27001 defines how an organization continually manages information security risks. Certification does not guarantee that security incidents will never occur.

sections.heading: IV. C27 | ISO/IEC 27005:2022: how is risk management carried out?

body.text: 1. The difference between ISO 27001 and ISO 27005
This is a central distinction in this unit.
ISO 27001 requires an organization to establish appropriate information security risk assessment and treatment processes.
ISO 27005 further supports the organization in designing, carrying out, and repeatedly improving those processes.

The formal title of ISO/IEC 27005:2022 is Guidance on Managing Information Security Risks. The fourth edition was published in October 2022 and works with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and the ISO 31000:2018 risk management framework.
2. The complete ISO 27005 management process

rows: Define the organization, scope, risk criteria, and assessment method
Identify risk scenarios and risk owners
Analyze consequences, likelihood, and risk levels
Compare against acceptance criteria and prioritize
Select controls, treat risks, and establish residual risk
Retain necessary process and results information

body.text: These references follow the actual clause structure of ISO/IEC 27005:2022.
Risk assessment must be updated as technology, threats, business activities, and control effectiveness change; completing a spreadsheet once a year does not complete the process.
3. Semiconductor example: how can we establish a risk register?
A Risk Register is a practical artifact of risk management.
Suppose that a company identifies three risks:

rows: Misuse of an equipment maintenance account interrupts production
Customer design data is improperly accessed across tenants
A low-impact configuration weakness on the corporate website

body.text: These numbers use the earlier example matrix with categories from 1 to 5. They are neither a real company assessment nor official ISO scores.
ISO 27005 then helps us ask more detailed questions.

R-001: can an attacker actually reach the equipment management interface? Is it reachable externally, accessible only through a maintenance jump host, or available only inside the fab? Different conditions change likelihood.
R-002: what happens if the data is disclosed? Consequences may involve customer contracts, intellectual property, trade secrets, reputation, and cross-border data processing obligations.

R-003: does low risk mean that treatment is unnecessary? Not necessarily. Consider legal and contractual requirements, whether the weakness can be chained with others, and the risk acceptance criteria.
The risk register should therefore also record treatment measures, target dates, evidence, residual risk, acceptance or escalation decisions, and the next review date.
4. Why are CVSS or vulnerability severity alone insufficient?
This question requires reasoning about business context.
Suppose that two systems have the same high-severity vulnerability:

items: System A is isolated laboratory equipment without a normal reachable network path.
System B is an internet-facing SaaS service processing substantial customer data.

body.text: The vulnerability's technical severity alone cannot establish the actual business risk of either system.
We also need attack reachability in the environment, controls, business consequences, and any alternative attack paths.

MITRE ATT&CK helps describe attacker techniques. For example, T1190, Exploit Public-Facing Application, and T1078, Valid Accounts, cover exploitation of public-facing services and misuse of valid accounts, respectively.
The OWASP Risk Rating Methodology provides an application risk analysis method that considers threat agents, vulnerabilities, likelihood, and impact.
Distinguish their roles:

rows: Analyze and test application weaknesses and risks
Manage information security risks at the organizational level
Provide a structured method for risk assessment

body.text: An ATT&CK technique list does not directly establish the probability of an attack. An OWASP application risk score should not be treated as a measure of all enterprise business risks.
5. Who is authorized to accept residual risk?
Suppose that the treatment for R-001 adds maintenance procedures to a wafer fab and reduces equipment availability.
Engineers may implement controls, the security team performs assessment, and manufacturing must weigh the production consequences.
Under ISO 27001 Clause 6.1.3 and ISO 27005 Clause 8, an appropriate risk owner must approve the risk treatment plan and acceptance of residual risk.
The implication is:
Experts can analyze risk, but authority to decide whether to bear it must match the organization's authorization, responsibilities, and governance arrangements.
Legal compliance and personnel safety risks cannot be reduced to an assumption that a manager's signature permits acceptance of any consequence.

sections.heading: V. C28 | ISO/IEC 27002:2022: which controls should follow risk identification?

body.text: 1. ISO 27002 provides practical guidance on security controls
Suppose that ISO 27005 has helped a semiconductor company identify a risk:
“An external equipment supplier's maintenance account has excessive access privileges.”
The next question is:
Which controls should we implement?
ISO/IEC 27002:2022 provides practical guidance on information security controls. It is not a standard for obtaining standalone ISO/IEC 27002 management-system certification.
2. The 93 controls in ISO 27002:2022
The 2022 edition organizes controls into four categories.

body.name: controlcounts
body.caption: ISO/IEC 27002: distribution of 93 controls
body.description: Bars show actual proportions of 37/93, 8/93, 14/93 and 34/93; counts do not indicate importance. There are 93 controls in total.

body.text: The distribution follows the standard editors' explanation in the official ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 27 journal.
The four categories serve the following purposes:

rows: Security policies, supplier management, information asset management
Security awareness, employee responsibilities, termination arrangements
Access restrictions, secure areas, equipment protection
Access control, encryption, logging, backup, network security

body.text: These categories connect directly to the security control classifications in C17–C21.
3. How can three industries select specific controls?
Taiwanese semiconductors: supply-chain access risk
Relevant controls include:

items: 5.19 — Information Security in Supplier Relationships
5.21 — Managing Information Security in the ICT Supply Chain
5.15 — Access Control
5.18 — Access Rights

body.text: These controls can support supplier access management, least privilege, periodic access reviews, and allocation of security responsibilities.

SEMI E187 provides a technical industry baseline for operating systems, network security, endpoint protection, and logging in semiconductor manufacturing equipment. In 2026, SEMI is also advancing E187 revision work with further levels of requirements.
US Silicon Valley: cloud-platform risk
Relevant controls include:

items: 5.23 — Information Security for Use of Cloud Services
8.24 — Use of Cryptography
8.15 — Logging

body.text: Examples include a cloud-provider assessment process, clarification of shared responsibilities, encryption of sensitive information, and retention of sufficient operation logs.
ISO 27002 Control 5.23 specifically addresses selecting, using, managing, and exiting cloud services.
Taiwanese finance: transaction and operational risk
Relevant controls include:

items: 5.30 — ICT Readiness for Business Continuity
5.24 — Information Security Incident Management Planning and Preparation
8.13 — Information Backup

body.text: These controls can help financial institutions prepare for system interruptions, establish recovery readiness, and manage backups.

Legal risk-management obligations still depend on the applicable Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) rules. Each ISO 27002 recommendation cannot simply be treated as a mandatory domestic legal provision.
4. Are ISO 27001 Annex A and ISO 27002 the same document?
No.
Their control structures correspond, but the documents serve different purposes.
ISO 27001 Annex A provides a reference control list for checking that necessary information security controls have not been omitted.
ISO 27002 provides the purposes of the corresponding controls and more detailed implementation guidance.
A company can therefore select controls based on its risks and use ISO 27002 to design their implementation.
This also explains why implementing ISO 27001 does not make every ISO 27002 recommendation applicable without qualification.
C28's central concept: ISO 27002 guides control selection and implementation. The need for a particular control depends on risk, business requirements, and applicable law.

sections.heading: VI. C29 | ISO/IEC 27701: how do information security and privacy management differ?

body.text: 1. Secure data can still be processed improperly
Suppose that a Silicon Valley technology company develops an AI service.
The company encrypts all customer data and implements MFA, network firewalls, and backups.
These measures can reduce the risk of unauthorized access to or destruction of data.
However, the company might still collect excessive personal information, retain it longer than necessary, or use it for purposes that were not properly disclosed.
Such problems may involve privacy governance even without a conventional hacking incident.
Distinguish the two areas:

rows: Is personal information collected, used, and managed appropriately?
Focuses on CIA and information-related risks
Focuses on lawful processing, purposes, and individuals' rights and interests
Example: limiting unnecessary collection and retention

body.text: The areas overlap, but one cannot replace the other.
NIST Privacy Framework 1.0 also treats the effects of data processing on individuals as an important consideration in organizational privacy risk management.
2. What is a PIMS?
PIMS stands for Privacy Information Management System.
It helps organizations manage Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
Distinguish two roles:
PII Controller: the party that determines the purposes and principal means of processing personal information.
PII Processor: a party that processes personal information on behalf of a controller and following its instructions.
Suppose that a Taiwanese bank decides which customer information to collect for credit assessment and commissions a technology supplier to process the data.
Where the actual arrangement matches these roles, the bank may be the controller and the supplier the processor.
This simplified scenario introduces PIMS. The actual roles depend on the data-processing relationship and applicable law.
3. What changed between ISO 27701:2019 and 27701:2025?
Understand this edition change.

ISO confirms that the 2025 edition can function as an independent management-system standard. Japan's Information Management System Accreditation Center (ISMS-AC) also explains the change from the original ISMS-PIMS certification structure to independent PIMS certification.
For CEH study, remember two points:
First, the original question uses the 2019 edition, so understand its role as an extension at that time.
Second, current enterprise implementation should use the independent PIMS structure in the 2025 edition and account for transition arrangements for existing certifications.
4. Silicon Valley: how does ISO 27701 connect with California privacy law?
Suppose that a SaaS company provides an AI customer-service platform and collects names, email addresses, and operation logs.

Where the business and processing fall within the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), including subsequent CPRA amendments, Civil Code §1798.100 imposes obligations concerning collection, purposes, retention, and reasonable security.

Section 1798.100(c) requires collection, use, retention, and sharing to be reasonably necessary and proportionate to the applicable purposes. Section 1798.100(e) addresses appropriate security procedures and practices.
ISO 27701 can help establish management mechanisms and evidence. PIMS certification does not automatically establish full compliance with every California legal requirement.
5. Taiwanese finance: personal-data risks extend beyond disclosure
Suppose that a bank uses AI for credit assessment.
Even without a data breach, it must examine:

items: Whether customer data use satisfies the specific purpose and lawful processing conditions.
Whether it obtains data unrelated to the business purpose.
Whether data is retained only for the necessary period.
Whether external processors are managed appropriately.
Whether it can handle individuals' legally established rights requests.

body.text: Articles 19 and 20 of Taiwan's Personal Data Protection Act govern the conditions for collection, processing, and use of personal data by non-government agencies. Article 12 of the Enforcement Rules lists measures related to data security, risk assessment, and management.

Some provisions amended on November 11, 2025 remain awaiting commencement. Articles 11, 19 and 20 cited here are not in that amendment's pending-effect list. A compliance decision must still use the provisions in force at the time of the conduct and the applicable rules.
C29's central concept: ISO 27701 manages personal-data processing and privacy risks. ISO 27001 addresses broader information security management requirements.

sections.heading: VII. Integrated practice: risk management and requirements in three industries

body.text: We can now place the five concepts within enterprise governance.
Case A | Taiwanese semiconductors: equipment suppliers' remote-maintenance risk
Business context: a semiconductor manufacturer depends on external equipment suppliers for maintenance. Suppliers need remote access to some equipment management systems.
Risk: misuse of supplier accounts could allow unauthorized people to obtain manufacturing process information or alter equipment settings, affecting confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

rows: Define ISMS scope, responsibilities, and policies for equipment maintenance systems
Identify maintenance channels, accounts, suppliers, and process consequences
Supplier management, least privilege, access logs
Establish network, endpoint, and monitoring baselines according to equipment type
Confirm reasonable secrecy measures for information involving trade secrets

body.text: SEMI confirms that E187 focuses on semiconductor equipment operating systems, network security, endpoint protection, and security monitoring. Compliance obligations may arise from procurement contracts, customer requirements, or internal arrangements. It does not follow that every semiconductor company automatically has the same statutory certification obligation.
Case B | US Silicon Valley: tenant isolation in an AI SaaS platform
Business context: a Silicon Valley company provides AI document analysis to several enterprises.
Risk: the backend API does not correctly check which customer owns a document, potentially allowing customer A to obtain customer B's information.
Technical analysis can refer to API1: Broken Object Level Authorization in the OWASP API Security Top 10 2023.
Management responsibilities can be divided as follows:

rows: Assess likelihood and impact of cross-tenant exposure

Case C | Taiwanese financial institution: introducing third-party AI
Business context: a Taiwanese bank plans to use a third-party AI service to help prepare credit-analysis reports.
Risks include improper disclosure of sensitive customer information, incorrect AI output, excessive supplier maintenance privileges, and system failures affecting the business.
How should ISO standards and FSC supervisory rules work together?
The FSC's Regulations Governing the Implementation of Internal Control and Audit Systems of Financial Holding Companies and Banking Industries provide directly relevant arrangements:

rows: Establish internal-control and risk-management policies and procedures
Establish the three-lines model for internal control
Risk assessment, control activities, information and communication, and monitoring

body.text: These provisions are drawn from the official FSC legal system. Under Article 55, the May 6, 2026 amendment took effect on publication, with commencement of Articles 44–47 separately determined by the competent authority. The table's Articles 4, 9, 10, 20, 21, 24 and 25 are outside that deferred group. An actual case must still use the version applicable at the time of conduct.

In addition, on March 5, 2026 the Bankers Association published its Financial Institutions' Information and Communication Systems and Services Supply Chain Risk Management Rules, which may provide a self-regulatory basis for third-party technology and supply-chain security management.
A bank's review should therefore go beyond asking whether a supplier holds ISO 27001 certification.

Examine whether the actual service falls within the certified scope, how bank data is accessed and retained, whether the supplier can provide evidence of control effectiveness, how incidents are reported, and which authorized level within the bank bears residual risk.

sections.heading: XI. Integrated understanding check: one case spanning C25–C29

body.text: No model answers are supplied here. First test whether you can apply the five concepts to one complex decision.
Scenario: Taiwanese semiconductor company × US AI SaaS provider × Taiwanese financial institution
A Taiwanese semiconductor company uses a Silicon Valley AI SaaS service to analyze equipment maintenance data and supplies some financial and equipment information to a bank for credit assessment.
The company is ISO/IEC 27001:2022-certified, but the new project reveals the following:
Event A: the SaaS platform's API might allow one customer to read another customer's equipment maintenance records.
Event B: the semiconductor equipment supplier uses long-lived remote-maintenance accounts without appropriate separation of privileges or periodic review.
Event C: the AI platform additionally retains employee names, contact details, and equipment operation records. Some data has no clear relationship with the original analytical purpose.

Event D: the security team uses a 5×5 matrix and scores A at 20, B at 15, and C at 10. Management believes A must be more important than B and requires every department to allocate its budget solely by risk score.
Event E: the US SaaS supplier states, “We have ISO 27001 certification, so we do not need to provide additional security control evidence.”
Answer these six questions:

1. C25 — Risk analysis: for A, B, and C, develop a complete Risk Scenario identifying assets, threats, vulnerabilities, potential impacts, and the Risk Owner. How would you assess whether D's ranking is reasonable?
2. C26 — ISO 27001: how should the new project establish whether it falls within the existing ISMS certification scope? Which risk assessment, SoA, or other records need updating?
3. C27 — ISO 27005: for B, design a complete process covering identification, analysis, evaluation, treatment, and subsequent review. Explain which evidence is needed at each stage.
4. C28 — ISO 27002: select appropriate security controls for A and B, explain how they work and how to verify them, and explain why they reduce the relevant risks.
5. C29 — ISO 27701: why is C more than an information security issue? How should the roles of ISO 27001, ISO 27701:2019, and ISO 27701:2025 be distinguished?

6. Cross-industry governance: as security-review lead for the three-party project, how would you distinguish the authority and applicability of Taiwan's Trade Secrets Act, California personal-data law, FSC regulations, SEMI E187, ISO standards, and the Bankers Association's self-regulatory rules? What practical evidence would you request in response to E?
The intended capability is to identify risks, support decisions with evidence, translate those decisions into controls, and continually verify whether the controls work.
Independently completing this integrated case connects C25–C29's CEH foundations with enterprise risk governance, ISO management systems, and cross-industry compliance practice.
